Deleting your alerts:

  1. Open the main menu.
  2. Select Search Alerts from the drop-down list.
  3. You’ll be brought to a list of all of your alerts. Tap and hold over the one you’d like to delete.
  4. Tap and hold over the alert you want to delete until it turns grey and the delete button (rubbish bin) appears at the top of the screen.
  5. Select all of the alerts you’d like to remove.

Not receiving your Alert emails? Make sure that you check your junk and/or spam filters and add mail@info.gumtree.com and noreply@gumtree.com to your safe senders list.

Title: Creating & Managing Alerts
Summary: Learn how to set up, edit, and delete alerts.
Description__c:
Search alerts are a great way to find and snap up specific items. By setting up alerts, you will be notified when new and relevant ads have been added to the site.

Creating your alert:

  1. Enter a category, keywords and a location in the search bar.
  2. Click Go.
  3. Once you’re satisfied that the search is returning the results you’d like to set an alert for, click Set Search Alert on the left side of the page.

You should now see your alert within the My Alerts page. Alert emails are sent out every day if there are new results. If there are no new results, an alert will not be sent out.

Editing your alerts:

  1. Open the user menu .
  2. Select My Alerts from the drop-down list.
  3. You’ll be brought to a list of all of your alerts. Under the description of each is the toggle on/off button. To turn an alert off (but not delete it) click on the toggle. To turn it back on, simply click the toggle again at any point.

Deleting your alerts:

  1. Open the user menu .
  2. Select My Alerts from the drop-down list.
  3. Click Delete  next to the alert you’d like to remove. If you want to delete all of your alerts at the same time, you can click Delete All at the top of the list.

Not receiving your Alert emails? Make sure that you check your junk and/or spam filters and add mail@info.gumtree.com and noreply@gumtree.com to your safe senders list.

Title: Can I Turn Off Email Messages?
Summary: Learn how to stop receiving emails from other users, and set up your phone number.
Description__c:
All ads on Gumtree need at least one way to contact the seller. If you don’t want to be contacted through our masked email system, you can supply a phone number instead.

To disable Gumtree messages:

  1. Login to your account and click on the user menu  at the top of the page.
  2. Select Manage My Ads from the drop-down menu.
  3. Find the ad you want to remove your email from and click Edit  on that ad.
  4. Scroll down to the Your Contact Details section. Uncheck the Email box and then check the Phone box. Enter your phone number into the Phone field.
  5. Click Update My Ad.

Note: This will only edit your contact details on one ad. To change your contact details on all of your ads, you must repeat the steps above for each of your ads. When posting ads in the future, make sure to double check your contact details before posting.

Title: Safety in Messages
Summary: Learn how to tell when a message may be a scam or an attempt to commit fraud.
Description__c:
When sending messages through Gumtree, we mask your email on top of other safeguards to try to ensure that every interaction you have is with a genuine member of the site. Despite these safeguards, it’s important to know the warning signs when buying and trading online.

They Move the Conversation to a New Platform

To avoid our security systems fraudsters will often request that you leave Gumtree and contact them through a private platform. If they ask you to reply to their personal email address instead of their masked Gumtree email, be cautious.

Note: Sometimes these requests can be legitimate, but if they refuse to speak anywhere other than through private email, it might be best to move on. Ask them to speak directly over the phone if they don’t want to use Gumtree messages.

They Can’t Meet In Person

Fraudsters will often work remotely. This is partly because they need to cast a wide net to make money and partly for their own safety. They may have an elaborate excuse that makes them sound legitimate. Some common stories are that they work in an offshore oil rig, that they’re a member of the military, or that they’re buying a special present for a family member from overseas.

They Rush the Process

Fraudsters want to rush people through the scam before they begin to catch on. They’ll often send long-winded, overly detailed messages trying to finish the transaction. If you’re the buyer, they’ll start sending information on how to pay them right away. If you’re the seller, they may ask a few basic questions in the same message before instructing you on how to collect their payment.

They Skip Details

Since fraudsters aren’t actually looking to buy or sell anything, they don’t usually ask any item-specific questions. If they do ask questions, they’ll be rushed and very basic.

In many cases, they’re also using pre-written responses that don’t mention the exact type of item in their reply. They may use general terms like ‘the item’ or ‘your vehicle.’ In some cases, they simply copy and paste the ad title into the message to make it appear specific. For example: ‘I would like to buy your Honda Civic 2016 Blue.’

Too Good to be True Deals

In order to try and lure people into their scam, fraudsters will offer a deal that’s hard to refuse. If you’re the buyer and offer less than their asking price, they’ll accept on the first email. After all, they’re losing nothing in this deal unless you walk away.

If you’re selling the item, they may offer you more than asking price, or may want to buy everything you have for sale all at once. They may even offer extra if you remove the ad right away to ‘ensure the sale.’

Odd Payment Requests

Since fraudsters don’t usually meet in person, they need the money digitally. They may ask that you send them money through a method with no guarantees. Favourites include MoneyGram, Western Union, and other types of money transfer. They may also request payment through PayPal but insist that you use the Friends & Family setting so that you are offered less protection.

Scams aimed at buyers are generally simple, but there are two types:

  • They ask you to pay for the item before you meet up.
  • They ask for a deposit for an item you haven’t seen.

There are 3 main types of scams aimed at sellers:

  • They insist that you ship the item to them before payment.
  • They send you a payment notification or receipt and ask you to transfer some funds back to them before the full payment comes through.
  • They send you a fake payment notification or receipt, then ask you to transfer some of that money to a shipping company. Not only do they tell you which company to use for the transfer, but also which account number.

If you see any of these signs, don’t proceed any further with the transaction and reach out to our customer support team to let us know.

Title: Managing Gumtree Emails
Summary: Learn how to unsubscribe from Gumtree marketing emails.
Description__c:
Gumtree's emails feature listings, categories, and tips on how to make the most of your Gumtree experience – tailored just for you. From what's for sale in your area and trending up to how to make or save cash, Gumtree emails keep you first in line to find what you're looking for.

If you don't want these types of emails, you can unsubscribe at any time in two different ways. All of our marketing emails have a ‘click here to unsubscribe’ button at the bottom of the email. Clicking it will remove you from that mailing list.

You can also unsubscribe by following the steps below:

  1. Login to your account and click on the user menu  at the top of the page.
  2. Select My Details.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of the page. Under the heading Marketing preferences, you'll see 2 options.
  4. To stop receiving marketing emails from Gumtree, click the On/Off button next to ‘I would like to receive news, offers and promotions from Gumtree.’ It should now say ‘Off.’

If you'd like to re-subscribe, follow the same steps but make sure the button says ‘On.’

Alert Emails

You can turn alerts off at any time by clicking the 'click here to deactivate this alert' button found at the bottom of each alert email. If you want to manage multiple alerts at the same time, follow the steps in our Creating & Managing Alerts article.

Message Emails

There is no way to unsubscribe from email messages sent by buyers and sellers. However, you can change the contact method on your ad to phone only. To remove your email, edit your ad and uncheck the email option at the bottom of the ad page. For more help, read our Can I Turn off Email Messages article.

Title: Adding Videos
Summary: Learn how to upload and link a YouTube video to your ads.
Description__c:
Including a video with your ad could help you stand out and get more replies to your listing. Whether you’re giving buyers a video-tour of your vehicle or posting a commercial for your company, videos can be a great way to tell buyers more about your ad in an engaging way.

Currently, Gumtree is only able to link YouTube videos. To upload a video to YouTube, follow YouTube’s upload instructions. If you want to link to a video on a different platform, include the URL link in the description section of your ad.

To link a YouTube video:

  1. From the post ad or edit ad page, scroll down to the Media section.
  2. Add the video’s link into the YouTube Link field. Make sure to include the full URL link, including the https:// information.
  3. Confirm the changes to your ad at the bottom of the page.

Please remember to keep your video family friendly. Once uploaded, videos can be viewed from the ad’s page.

Note: This feature is not currently available in app.

Title: Adding Photos
Summary: Learn how to upload images to your ads. Learning how to add pictures is the best way to increase views on your ads.
Description__c:
Photos are the first part of an ad that most buyers see. Adding clear, detailed pictures draws buyers into your ad and saves you time answering questions that could be answered with a photo. Gumtree allows up to 20 images on each ad. Don’t be afraid to use them all.

Tips when taking photos:

  • Use bright lighting and uncluttered backgrounds.
  • Take photos of your item from different angles so buyers can get a 360 degree look.
  • The larger the item you’re selling, the more photos you should take.

To add photos:

  1. If you’re posting a new ad, tap Post an Ad. If you’re editing an existing ad, tap Edit  on the ad you’d like to update.
  2. Scroll down to the Images section.
  3. Click Add Image to choose photos from your file browser or click and drag images directly over top of the Add Image button.
  4. When the delete  button appears in the corner of the image, it has finished uploading.

To delete photos:

  1. From the post or edit ad screen, scroll down to the Images section.
  2. Click the delete  button in the corner of each photo to remove it.
  3. If you're editing, save your changes by clicking Update My Ad at the bottom of the screen.

Cover Photo/Image order: 

As a Gumtree user, when creating an ad, you have the ability to select a cover photo for your ad, by dragging it to the first position of all your images. This should save as your co ver image once your ad is live. In some instances users have reported that when they load a new ad, the cover photo is different to the one originally selected.
If this happens, please follow these steps:
  1. Go to the Manage my Ads/ My Gumtree tab
  2. View active ads
  3. On the ad you want to correct, click Edit  which will be on the top right hand corner of the ad, next to the Stats and Delete options.
  4. The edit ad flow should open with the original selected image order and cover photo
  5. Scroll down and select "Update My Ad" at the bottom
  6. Your cover photo should have updated and the Photos should be uploaded in the order you want them to appear on your ad. 

Please note that Gumtree will automatically delete all images from ads that have been inactive for 6 months or more.

Having trouble?

If you’re unable to upload your photos, read our I Can't Add Photos article for help.

Title: Sorting Search Results
Summary: Learn how to use Gumtree’s sorting options to take more control over your search results and change the ad ranking.
Description__c:
Ad ranking is where each ad appears on the page of search results. In a default search, ads are sorted by their posted date with the most recent ads showing at the top of the page, below the Featured ads section.

The Sort By drop-down menu can be found on the right-hand side of the page. This menu has 4 options:

  • Most recent first (default)
  • Price: low to high
  • Price: high to low
  • Nearest First

Once you change this setting it will be saved for your future searches. If it doesn’t save, you may need to allow Gumtree to store cookies on your browser. If you’re still having trouble, try clearing your cookies and updating your browser.

Title: Searching in Jobs
Summary: Learn how to use our search function to find your next job fast.
Description__c:
Whether you’re browsing just to see what’s out there or narrowing in on that dream job with laser-point precision, learning how to use the full power of our search filters will make searching much easier.

Browse vs. Search

The Browse and Search functions both filter through the same ads on Gumtree Jobs. However, both options have unique capabilities that are suited to different types of searches.

Browse allows for more casual searching. You can choose between Sector and/or Job Title, and choose 1 option under each filter type. It also has quick ways to broaden your search if there aren’t enough results.

Search allows you to select as many options under each filter as you’d like, allowing you to search multiple sectors, salaries, etc., and any combination of them all. The Search tab also allows for more specific location options, including a ‘Homeworking’ option.

Finding Ads Effectively

Whether searching or browsing, there are a few tips that can help you find what you’re looking for:

Add lots of filters

Filters are the most effective search tool because employers are choosing from the same list you are when they create their ads. You should select a filter for every option unless you have no preference. If no filter is chosen, all ads will be shown. For example, if you don’t select one of the options in the Salary filter, jobs with any salary will be listed.

Don’t depend too heavily on keywords

Keyword searches work by looking through titles and descriptions and removing any ads that don’t contain those words. They can be a powerful tool, but sometimes you will run into issues when the poster uses a different word or phrase than you’re searching for. Spelling mistakes can also prevent an ad from showing up. For this reason, keywords are best added at the end; if regular filters don’t return specific enough results.

Choose a location

Unless you’re willing to relocate, you probably have a good idea of what area you need your new job to be in. Don’t forget to choose a location so that you’re not wasting time looking at ads that are too far away.

Don’t be afraid to mix it up

If you’re not finding what you’re looking for, don’t be afraid to remove the least necessary filters or change up your keywords. Sometimes it only takes a few small tweaks to find your dream job.

Title: Logging In to Gumtree Jobs

Title: I Can't Find My Featured Ad
Summary: Learn more about Featured Ads and some common issues users run into when searching for them on the site.
Description__c:
Once your ad is active, any purchased features will take effect right away. If you don’t see your ad listed as Featured, please note the following:

  • Each page of search results only shows a maximum of 5 Featured ads at a time. If there are more than 5 Featured ads in any given search, the order will be chosen randomly and the next set of 5 will be shown on the following page. Another 5 will be shown on the 3rd page, and so on until all Featured ads have been seen, at which point it will repeat.
  • Each time the page is refreshed or a new user searches, the order will be changed so that all Featured ads get an equal chance on the first page.
  • When you apply a Featured promotion, it creates a second version that will appear in the Featured section. You will still see the normal version of your ad moving throughout the queues. If you don’t see the Featured banner on your ad, you’re likely looking at the free version.

How to Check Quickly

To see your ad in the full queue, search by its location and category. Remember that the wider the search you enter, the more Featured ads it will include. Try searching your immediate suburb and the most specific category first. If you see it there, you can rest assured that it will be seen in wider searches as well. If it’s a busy category such as Motors, you may also need to add a keyword to find it right away.

You can see all Featured ads at once by looking under Filters, then Other Options and clicking Feature ads. In this view, Featured ads are shown in the order of the date they were posted instead of a rotational order.

If I Can’t See It on Page 1, How Will Anyone Else?

While it can be frustrating not to see your Featured ads on page 1 of every search, remember that they are rotated randomly for every search. This means that your ad will still be seen at the top of page 1 for many users, even if you don’t see it there in the first few searches.

In searches where there are less than 5 Featured ads, your ad won’t just be at the top of page 1, it will be at the top of every page of search results.

When you click on a member’s profile, you can see up to 6 pieces of information:

  • Their chosen name
  • Their average response time
  • How long they’ve been posting ads on Gumtree
  • Whether or not they have any active ads
  • The reviews they’ve received from other members

Viewing A Buyer’s Profile

When a buyer sends you a message, you’ll be able to view their profile (if they have previous ratings). To see their profile:

  1. Go into your Message section.
  2. Select the message from the buyer whose profile you want to view.
  3. Click on the buyer’s name at the top of their message.

If you don't see any stars or can't click on their name, they don't have any ratings yet.

Viewing A Seller’s Profile

Whether you’re a buyer, or wanting to view your own seller profile, you can do so by following the steps below:

  1. Open the seller’s ad.
  2. On the right side, you’ll see the seller information section. From here you can see the most important parts of their profile.
  3. For more details, click View Profile.
  4. Use the tabs to toggle back and forth from Live ads to Reviews.

Missing Information

A user’s profile will be mostly blank if they’re new to Gumtree or don’t message other buyers or sellers very often. With each response sent, their averages will be determined. Once they’ve hit the enough replies to create a general average, it will appear on their profile.

What the law says

  • Postal address
  • Company registration number
  • VAT number
 
For the best results, add these details at the bottom of your ad.

You're more than welcome to list other similar items you have for sale in this category, but always follow the same rules.
 
Where can I promote my stock?
 
You can post ads in single and double beds, wardrobes, shelving and storage, mattresses, sofas and sofa beds. All our other categories are for private sellers.
 
Did you know? You can post one ad per item. We’ll take down any duplicates.
 
Use your business email

Remember to add your business details, too. This is part of our posting rules in the For Sale category, so make sure you're aware of it, otherwise we'll need to remove the ads and ask you to re-post them.

Title: PayPal Scams
Summary: Learn more about making payments through PayPal, and how to recognise dishonest PayPal requests.
Description__c:
We always recommend that all purchases on Gumtree be done face to face. However, if you don’t want to trade in cash PayPal can be a great option. Whenever you use an electronic transfer, it’s important to know how to use that method safely.

Know What Is or Isn’t Covered

PayPal has some default protections in place for both buyers and sellers. However, they are not available for all types of sales. Learn more about buyer and seller protection on PayPal's website.

Check Your Account

When selling, be sure to check your account after you’ve received the PayPal confirmation email. Don’t give the buyer the item until after the money has been fully deposited. If for any reason the money is on hold, it should show as on hold in your account.

Learn to Recognise Spoofs

Sometimes fraudsters will send emails that look like they’re from PayPal, but were actually created by the fraudster. These are called 'spoof' emails. You can see an example of this in the Real Scam Attempt Example section below.

Warning Signs

There are a number of warning signs during a scam attempt that it’s important to be able to recognise. For general red flags, see our Safety in Messages article. For PayPal requests, there a few specific things to watch out for.

Asking to use Friends & Family

The Family & Friends option on PayPal is meant to be used only with those you trust. Friends & Family payments do not have any seller or buyer protection from PayPal. If a buyer or seller asks you to use this method of payment, be cautious.

Claiming that the funds are on hold

PayPal can occasionally hold funds if it’s a larger amount, but they never hold funds on the condition that you confirm shipping or that you pay into another account first. If you receive an email that appears to be from PayPal mentioning these, don’t respond any further.

PayPal discourages contact

If you receive an email that looks like it’s from PayPal, but it tells you to follow up by replying directly through the email instead of on their website, be cautious.

Have you received a PayPal email that you’re not sure about? Contact PayPal to check whether or not it’s genuine.

Real Scam Attempt Example

Below is a copy of a real scam. If you’ve read this article and our Safety in Messages article, you should be able to see a few warning signs.

First Message

“Do you still have this?”

Second Message

“Great I'll buy it but I'll nt be able to come fr the pick up due to my disability. I'll arrange fr tht with a pick up guy.I'll make the payment through Pay Pal for the safety of both of us. I'll need your name, the pickup address & your pay pal email address for the payment. If you don't have pay pal account It's very easy and secured just visit their website and click on signup.”

Third Message

Hi _________,

You received a payment from _________. The money is pending and deposited in PayPal escrow account. The payment will not reflect in your account balance until we receive the proof of shipment from you for confirmation and, once shipment is confirmed, the money will be in your available balance within few minutes. This will help us continue to be a safer way to buy and sell.

How can I get my money sooner?

You should be able to get your money within few hours upon confirmation of shipment.

  • Send the item to the buyer’s postal address as displayed on this page.
  • Email us a proof of shipment such as shipment confirmation code/receipt reference number, this is required for shipment verification in other to transfer the money to your account immediately.
  • For items or services that cannot be physically delivered (for instance, digital goods like eBooks or smartphone apps), mark the order as Processed on the Transaction details page and provide any additional details requested.

Tip: The Tracking Number must be e-mailed directly to this email by using the reply button in your Mail Box and Quote the below Transaction IS for quick recognition of this transaction.

 

Were you able to spot all the red flags? Here’s a recap:

  • Bad spelling and grammar (even in the email from “PayPal”).
  • Wasn’t able to meet in person.
  • Long message that tries to move you through the process quickly. No negotiation or questions about the product.
  • Never mentioned the item they wanted to buy by name.
  • 'PayPal' asks you to confirm shipping with them before they will release funds.
  • 'PayPal' mentions multiple times to only respond by hitting reply on the email. No links to customer service or your account.

Title: Jobs Policies
Summary: Learn more about our policies when posting in the Jobs category on Gumtree
Description__c:
Along with our general posting policies, all Jobs posted on Gumtree must follow the policies below:

  • All Jobs ads must be for applicants over 16 years of age. Ads specifically requesting applicants under 16 are not permitted on Gumtree.
  • Generic postings advertising multiple different positions or employment services in a single ad are not allowed.
  • All job ads are required to include the salary band and location, as well as providing a detailed position description.
  • We do not accept postings which require down payments in any forms, including requiring candidates to send money or stamped, addressed envelopes to gain further details of the positions.
  • We do not accept postings that advertise for models or actors (either male or female) using generic (Hotmail, Yahoo, Gmail, etc.) email accounts and/or mobile phone numbers. These posters must include a registered agency email address and landline phone number.
  • We do not allow Job ads that require a photo in the application. Modeling or acting jobs are exempted from this policy, as long as they also fit the requirements described above.
  • All 'work from home' job offers must be posted using a business domain while also meeting all other job policy requirements.
  • Job offers taking place overseas must be paid in pound sterling and employment contracts must be signed at a local branch. The ads must state a local street address, valid phone number, a website, and as much information about the positions as possible to be compliant.
  • We do not allow jobs for adult, erotic, or sexual services of any kind. This includes but is not limited to: adult cleaning/lawn care, webcamming, adult modeling/photography, escort and prostitution.

Replying to Job Ads

  • Replies to ads for any purpose other than recruitment to a legitimate position are prohibited.
  • Replies to ads for personal reasons, or for solicitation of any sexual or otherwise inappropriate purposes are strictly prohibited and may result in a loss of ability to use Gumtree.

It is the responsibility of the advertiser posting an ad on Gumtree to ensure that content advertised adheres to all Gumtree posting policies as well as applicable laws. As a condition of your use of Gumtree specified under our Terms of Use, you agree that you will not violate any laws. For more of Gumtree’s policies, please read our General Posting Policies and What’s Not Allowed on Gumtree articles.

Title: Property Policies
Summary: Learn more about our policies when posting in the Property category.
Description__c:
Along with our general posting rules, all Property ads posted on Gumtree must follow the policies below:

Knowing your legal obligations

  • Users listing and replying to our Property ads are responsible for complying with all applicable laws and regulations.

  • When posting in Property, please ensure that you know your legal obligations. Property laws vary, depending on where the property is in the UK, and the type of tenancy or tenant. While we are not able to list every law or regulation in this article, failure to meet your legal obligations may result in your ad being removed from Gumtree.

Listings

  • Only one listing can be posted of the same room and/or property.
  • Each listing must only include details of one property.
  • Private landlords can post two active listings at one time. Users posting more than two active listings will be updated to an Agent Account and will be required to pay a fee for further ads.

  • Listings for rooms and/or properties that aren’t available to let or buy are not permitted.

  • All rooms and/or properties listed must be available to be viewed.

  • You must have the right to offer the property for rental/sale and will not breach any law, agreement or contract by doing so.

  • If you require consent from any third party (such as a mortgage supplier or freeholder) to market or let the property, you must have obtained the necessary consents.

Responsibilities

  • Landlords must comply with all responsibilities as laid out in England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

  • This includes, but is not limited to, giving a copy of your Landlord Gas Safety Record to tenants, ensuring electrical equipment is safely installed and protecting the tenant’s deposit in a government-approved scheme (for assured shorthold tenancies).

Professional landlords and real estate agents 

  • Professional landlords and real estate agents must select ‘Yes’ when asked ‘Are you acting as an agent?’. Posting as a non-business is misleading and therefore not allowed.

  • Listings from Professional landlords and real estate agents must meet National Trading Standards guidelines. This includes the property’s council tax band or rate and the property price and tenure information (for sales).

  • When posting ads for rentals, you may request the type of person you’re looking for, provided you do not discriminate on the basis of the applicable protected characteristics in the Equality Act 2010 (disability, gender reassignment, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation). 

  • Any ads which we are made aware of that violate the Equality Act will be removed. This includes “no DSS”, “no housing benefit” or any other ads that prohibit applications from those who rely on state benefits to pay some or all of their rent.

  • In addition, we do not allow listings that specify “no children”

Fees

  • Property owners in England and Wales may not request fees that are not permitted under the Tenant Fees Act 2019.

EPC requirements

  • All domestic rental properties are required to have an Energy Performance Certificate (EPC). All tenants must be provided with a free of charge copy of the property’s EPC.

  • Since April 2013, all properties rented in the private rental sector have been required to comply with the Minimum Level of Energy Efficiency standard (EPC band E)

Discounted / free accommodation

  • Listings that offer accommodation in exchange for services will be removed. 

  • This includes, but is not limited to, adverts that violate the Sexual Offences Act 2003 under which ‘sex for rent’ arrangements (discounted or free accommodation in return for sexual relations) are illegal.

Flatmates and people with lodgers 

  • When posting ads for flatmates or lodgers, you may request the type of person you are looking for if something called the “small premises exception” applies, provided you do not discriminate on the basis of race (which includes nationality). 

  • If you are expressing a preference in your ad, please give an explanation, by, for example, focusing on describing the people living in the property.

Additional considerations

  • If your property is outside the United Kingdom, it must be posted within either the Holiday Rentals or International subcategories.

  • Caravans may be advertised in Property > Holiday Rentals, depending on the length of the rental.

  • All income from self-employment over £1,000 or earnings of more than £2,500 from renting out property must be reported to HMRC.

Title: How Long Are Ads Active?
Summary: Learn more about run times, expiring ads, and how to repost your ads.
Description__c:

  • Ads in Community, Pets, Motors, Jobs and For Sale will be live for 30 days.

Once the ad’s run-time is up, we’ll send you an email notice that your ad is about to expire. You can apply a Bump Up at any time to reset its clock. If no Bump Up is applied, the ad will be removed from the queues and placed into your Inactive Ads list.

Inactive Ads

After you delete an ad or it expires, we save a copy of it in your Inactive Ads section. Inactive ads are not visible to anyone but you. We keep them for you so you can use them as a reference for future ads. We automatically delete images from inactives ads after 6 months. Inactive ads can't be deleted or removed from your list.

How to Repost Ads

After your ad expires, you can still repost it by applying a Bump Up. A Bump Up will put the ad back into the queues as if you’d created a whole new ad – without the hassle. Bumped Up ads will run for the same amount of time as they originally ran (30 or 60 days).

If you don’t want to apply a Bump Up you can still post your ad again, but it will have to be done by manually creating a new version.

Title: Avoiding Discrimination
Summary: Learn more about the Equalities Act, and how to stay within the law while posting.
Description__c:
Everyone wants and deserves to be treated fairly. In the UK, the Equalities Act 2010 protects our rights, giving us all equal access to employment and public and private services.


When you’re posting on Gumtree, it’s very important that your ad respects the law. You need to write your ads so that they don’t discriminate based on age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Know Your Rights and Responsibilities
The easy way to bring the spirit and the letter of the law to your posts is with this brilliant online tool from the Equality and Human Rights Commission. It helps you to find the guidance you need in almost every scenario, whether you’re posting or responding. And best of all, it’s free.

Focus on the Skills You’re After, Not the Person
When you’re writing your job description, focus on stating the skills you’re looking for. Don’t think about a particular type of person.

Report an Ad
At Gumtree, we rely on our community to help us keep everything as it should be. You can get involved by reporting an ad you want us to look at. We’ll work with its owner to help get it right.

Title: Vehicle History Check
Summary: Learn more about the Vehicle History Check and how it can help you buy with confidence.
Description__c:
Buying a car is exciting. But it can also be stressful. To help you avoid getting your fingers burned, we always run a Vehicle History Check when someone posts a vehicle ad. If it doesn’t pass, we don’t list it.

What We’ll Check:

  • If the car is listed as stolen on the Police National Computer
  • If the DVLA has recorded the vehicle as scrapped
  • If an insurer has written off the car because it’s either very damaged or stolen
  • If the DVLA has recorded the car as exported or imported.

What We Don’t Check:

  • Any mileage discrepancies
  • Any outstanding money owed that relates to previous sales

Take a look at our Vehicle Scams article for extra tips on staying safe with Gumtree.

Do Your Homework

We carry out the free Vehicle History Check when someone posts the ad on our site. Things can change in the time between the vehicle being posted and you viewing and deciding to buy. So always check that things still stack up.

We’ve put together lots of extra guidance to help ease your worries when buying a used vehicle. Head over to The Inside Track to get started.

Title: Rehoming Pets Online Safely
Summary: Learn more about what Gumtree does to protect pets, and where to find out more about buying online humanely.
Description__c:
We are a nation of animal lovers. When you rehome a pet online, you want to ensure that you’re buying from a safe, humane and honest seller.

At Gumtree, we’ve taken measures to try to ensure that all pets rehomed on our site are treated with their welfare in mind. One important step in that process is trying to go as far as possible to meet the 27 minimum standards set out by PAAG (Pet Advertising Advisory Group) for websites offering pets for sale via online adverts. These guidelines help ensure that safety standards are adhered to, and more animals are treated with respect and care.

Even though precautions have been taken, it is still important to be cautious when rehoming pets. That’s why some of the UK’s top animal welfare organisations, veterinary and industry bodies who make up the PAAG have united to help educate the public on spotting ads posted by dishonest pet sellers.

PAAG has launched a new website — www.HowToBuyAPet.co.uk — to help arm you with tips on how to spot an untrustworthy ad and questions to ask the seller. We encourage you to visit and read through their detailed and helpful guides.

Learn more about PAAG.

Title: People We Work With
Summary: Learn more about which organisations Gumtree partners with to ensure the success of our community.
Description__c:
At Gumtree, we’re always looking to improve the community experience on our site. With many different types of items for sale, we sometimes partner with trusted groups to lend us their expertise. These partnerships help us to ensure that we create a balanced platform for both buyers and sellers, while remaining a safe platform for all types of transactions.

Jobs

JobsAware was created by the Metropolitan Police as a non-profit organisation to help combat job scams for both job seekers and recruiters. JobsAware works with other organisations to help combat scams and exploitation – these include the Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy (BEIS), the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) and the Home Office, as well as National Trading Standards, the City of London Police and Action Fraud.

Vehicle Safe Trading Advisory Group (VSTAG)

The Vehicle Safe Trading Advisory Group is an industry forum created to protect users from fraud when buying or selling pre-owned vehicles online. VSTAG offers advice to both consumers and dealers, shares information between industry leaders, and develops best-practise guidelines for their members. They also work with various law enforcement agencies and regulatory authorities to reduce online fraud. Visit the VSTAG website to learn more.

Pet Advertising Advisory Group (PAAG)

The Pet Advertising Advisory Group, comprised of animal welfare organisations, trade associations, and veterinary bodies, was created to address concerns over online advertisement of pets for sale, rehoming, and exchange. PAAG works to raise awareness about pet safety, responsible buying and selling, and how to report possible cases of abuse. Visit the PAAG website for more information. For more information about how Gumtree works with PAAG, read our Buying Pets Online Safely article.

Action Fraud

Action Fraud is run by the City of London Police and works with the National Fraud Intelligence Bureau (NFIB). Together, they help to educate the public and support those who have been defrauded online. For more information about their organisation, or to file a report, visit Action Fraud’s website.

  • Get Safe Online (GSOL)
  • Cyber Aware
  • National Trading Standards
  • Citizens Advice
  • National Cyber Security Centre
  • Residential Landlords Association (RLA)

Title: I’m Not Receiving Replies
Summary: Learn more about why you may not be receiving all of your messages, and how to find the missing replies.
Description__c:
When someone sends you a message on Gumtree, you'll get two copies of the message. The first will be sent to the email you have set up as your primary email for Gumtree (not necessarily your login email). The second will be sent to the Messages section of your account.

I’m Not Receiving Messages in the Messages Section

Any message that is sent to your primary email will be automatically connected to your account. The only exception to this is if the message was from a business user or if it came from the Jobs category. If it did come from a business user or a Job poster, it will be an email only and will not appear in your Messages section in Gumtree.

If the email was from a regular user and you still can’t see it in your Messages section, you are likely in the wrong account. Double check what the primary email is in your My Details section. If it’s not the email that received the message, logout and find the account that is linked to the email that received the email message.

I’m Not Receiving Messages to My Email

There could be one of two issues if you’re not receiving messages to your email. First, check which email is listed as the primary email on your account (this could be different from your login email) and ensure that it matches the email address that you’re checking. You can see your primary email by clicking the user menu (Hello, followed by your username) and then selecting My Details. The email that appears under Primary email will be the email that receives your messages.

I'm Not Receiving Messages to My Email or in the Messages Section

If you’re not receiving messages in your email or your Messages section, it’s most likely that you haven’t received a reply yet. Patience is key. If you’re unsure, you can always ask a friend to send you a test message.

If you’re still having trouble after following the steps above, please contact our customer support team so we can investigate further.

Title: Clearing Cookies and Cache
Summary: Learn what cookies are, why they can cause problems, and how to clear them from your browser.
Description__c:
Browsers store information from websites in the form of cookies and a cache. This stored information helps web pages you’ve already visited load faster and remembers your personalized selections between visits (e.g., search location). Sometimes, this stored information can cause interference. If your browser is up to date and you’re still having trouble, try clearing your cookies and cache.

Follow the steps for your specific browser below:
 

Google Chrome

  1. Click on the 3-dot menu in the top right corner of the Google Chrome window.
  2. Select More Tools.
  3. Select Clear Browsing Data.
  4. Make sure that you’re in the Advanced section of the menu, then check Cookies and Other Site Data and Cached Images and Files. To avoid erasing any auto-filled passwords, make sure that Passwords and Autofill form data are unchecked.
  5. Click Clear Data.
  6. Close Google Chrome and restart your browser before trying Gumtree again.

For more information on Chrome, click here.
 

Mozilla Firefox

  1. Click the 3-line menu in the top right corner of the Firefox window.
  2. Select Library, followed by History.
  3. Click Clear Recent History.
  4. Change the Time range to clear menu to Everything.
  5. Make sure that only Cookies and Cache are selected.
  6. Click Clear Now.
  7. Close Firefox completely and restart before trying Gumtree again.

For more information on Firefox, click here.
 

Safari

  1. Click on the Safari menu in the top left corner of your screen.
  2. Select Preferences, then Privacy.
  3. Click on Manage Website Data.
  4. Find Gumtree in your list and select it.
  5. Click Remove.
  6. Click Done.
  7. Close Safari and restart your browser before trying Gumtree again.

For more information on Firefox, click here.
 

Edge

  1. Click on the 3-line menu in the top right corner of the Edge window.
  2. Select History, then Clear All History.
  3. Make sure that only Cookies and Cache are selected.
  4. Click Clear.
  5. Close Edge and restart your browser before trying Gumtree again.

For more information on Edge, click here.
 

Internet Explorer

For step by step instructions, check which version you’re currently using and then follow the instructions for your version of IE here.
 

Tip: Although we don’t recommend it for all issues, some browser problems can be bypassed by using the private browsing mode. To open a private window, click on your browser’s menu and select New Private Window. In Chrome, it’s called a New Incognito Window. If you’re using Edge, it’s a New InPrivate Window.

Title: Received an Email About an Ad I Didn't Post
Summary: Learn what may be the cause of an ad you didn’t create appearing on your account.
Description__c:
Whenever an ad is posted on your account, we’ll send an email to your account’s Primary email address to let you know. If you unexpectedly receive an email from Gumtree confirming that you just posted an ad, but you did not actually post the ad, then someone else may have gained access to your account. Fraudsters will sometimes take over genuine seller’s accounts to attempt to defraud the community.

If someone has gained access to your Gumtree account, follow the steps below:

  1. Sign in to your Gumtree account immediately and write down the Ad ID numbers of any ads on your account that you didn’t post. After noting the Ad IDs, delete the ads. Please also check your own ads to ensure that nothing was changed. For help with this step, read our How to Edit an Ad or How to Delete an Ad article.
  2. Contact our customer support team and provide the Ad ID numbers of the falsely posted ads. A member of our team will then be able to reset your account and walk you through the process of regaining control.

How Fraudsters Gain Access to An Account

Gumtree accounts are most often accessed through a method called phishing. Phishing is a process where fraudsters send others fake emails that look like they are from Gumtree. They may also appear as pop-up ads. They will then ask you to sign in via a fake Gumtree site, or request that you tell them your password. Once you’ve entered your email and password, they can use these details on the real Gumtree site to access your account.

Note: Gumtree customer support will never ask for your password. If you receive an email asking for your account password, this is a phishing attempt.

To ensure that you do not fall for phishing attacks, learn to recognise phishing emails and always make sure that you’re logging in to the real Gumtree site. When you login to Gumtree the address in your web browser should look like this: https://my.gumtree.com/login

Title: What to Do If I’ve Been Scammed
Summary: Learn what steps to take if you’ve been the victim of fraud.
Description__c:
Whether you've been defrauded by someone or you think you've discovered stolen goods, you should always contact your local police to report the incident and get a reference number. If the police take the matter further, the investigating police officer will contact us. We'll do all we can to provide the police with any information that helps their investigation.

Before You Go to the Police

If your item hasn't arrived, it may not be a case of fraud or stolen goods. It could be that you're just dealing with a seller who is slow to send an item or keep in contact. In either of these cases, please try contacting the seller directly one more time to resolve your problem.

Is It a Crime?

If you report your case to the police, they'll decide if it should be investigated as a crime or civil dispute. If the police feel that your case doesn't involve a criminal intent by the other party, they may advise you to take your own civil action to recover your losses. This is done through a local court or tribunal, which deals with small claims. For this, you'll need to know the name and address of the other party. A police officer will be able to help you with this process.

How Do I Make a Police Report?

The simplest way is to go to your local police station or call the local police operator on a non-emergency number. In most cases, your report can be taken by telephone and followed up later. To report fraud and cybercrime, you can also file a report online through Action Fraud.

What Evidence Do I Need?

The police may need these from you:

  • Essential details such as the nature, date and time of the offence
  • The name and contact details of the victim and suspect(s)
  • Any email exchanges between you and other person
  • If relevant, the Ad reference number or a printed copy of the Ad on Gumtree

If you decide to report a fraud to the Police, please get them to contact us. The majority of the police have our direct email and if they don't, ask them to contact us through the Help Desk. Gumtree is happy to help the police in their investigations once you've reported it.

Should I contact my bank?

If you are worried someone might have access to your bank account, contact your bank immediately.

When you contact your bank, they will take action straight away to protect your account so no more money can be taken. Your bank should normally refund the money if you haven't authorised a payment - as long as you haven't acted fraudulently, with intent or gross negligence.

What if I mistakenly sent money to a scammer?

Contact your bank straight away. Most UK banks have signed a voluntary agreement to reimburse money transferred because of a scam. Your bank will advise next steps but it is likely you will need to show:

  • You followed any security warnings from you bank
  • You believed the transaction was genuine
  • You weren’t being careless when you made the payment

Title: Photo Upload Issues
Summary: Learn what types of images can be uploaded to Gumtree and how to fix some common issues.
Description__c:
There can be a number of issues that interfere with uploading images to the site. If you’re having trouble, try the following:

  • Check the size of your images. Each individual photo must be under 8 MB. If your photos are over 8 MB, reduce the size and try again. 
  • Check the format of the images. Gumtree accepts JPEG and PNG. If your image is not one of these formats, you will need to convert it before uploading. 
  • Make sure your web browser isn’t interfering. 


Tip: If you’re not sure how to resize an image or change its format, here’s an easy online tool that will help: https://www.iloveimg.com/
 

Out of Order Photos

Photos should be uploaded in the order you want them to appear on your ad. If you’d like to change the order, you will need to edit your ad, remove the photos and reupload them in the new order. Click here for our guide on editing your ad.

If you’re using the app, you can reorder your photos by clicking and dragging them into the preferred position.

 

Cover Photo not appearing in the correct order. 

As a Gumtree user, when creating an ad, you have the ability to select a cover photo for your ad, by dragging it to the first position of all your images. This should save as your cover image once your ad is live.
In some instances users have reported that when they load a new ad, the cover photo is different to the one they had selected. If this happens, please follow these steps:

  • Go to the Manage my Ads/My Gumtree tab
  • View all active ads
  • On the ad you want to correct, click the "Edit" which will be on the top right hand corner of the ad, between the Stats and Delete options.
  • The edit ad flow should open with the original selected image order and cover photo

  • Your images should have updated and the Photos should be uploaded in the order you want them to appear on your ad. If you’d like to change the order, you will need to edit your ad, remove the photos and reupload them in the new order.

Title: I Can’t Send Replies
Summary: Learn why you may be having trouble sending replies or why your messages may be disappearing.
Description__c:
When you send a message to a buyer or seller, it will appear in the Messages section of your account. If other users are not receiving your messages, there are a few possible causes.

Your Message Was Blocked

If your message contained profanity, a violation of Gumtree policies, or if it appeared to be spam, it may have been blocked by our system. To avoid this, try re-wording your reply, ensuring it meets with our Ad Reply Code of Conduct.

Your Message Failed to Send

If you received an error when you tried to send a message, or if you’re sure that your reply wasn’t removed for the reasons described above, it may have run into a technical issue. Outdated browsers or issues with browser cookies can sometimes cause this. Try our troubleshooting steps in the Fixing Browser Issues article.

You’ve Changed Your Email Recently

If you’ve changed your email recently, you may have trouble when sending new messages to old conversations. You could also have trouble responding to buyers if you posted the ad before the email change.

You’re Responding to Someone Else’s Ad

If you’re sending messages back and forth with a poster and change emails mid-conversation, you may not be able to send a new message through the same conversation. To fix this, open a new conversation with the seller on the same ad.

You’re Replying to a Message About Your Own Ad

Once you post an ad, that ad is locked to your email address. If you edit your primary email while you have an ad live, you won't be able to send emails about that ad. You will still be able to receive messages to your new email, but you won’t be able to reply. Editing the email within the ad will not fix this issue. To be able to reply, your ads must be deleted and reposted after editing your primary email address.

Title: Tips on buying a bike
Summary: Our guide on buying a bike safely on Gumtree.
Description__c:
Buying a bike can make life fun, social and healthy. But sometimes it’s tricky to get your hands on a good one. Here are three tips to help you find the bike that’s right for you, and keep it safe:
 
  1. Make sure the bike isn’t stolen
Like with all purchases: if it seems too good to be true, it probably is. If it’s too cheap, there’s no paperwork or the seller is in a big rush to sell, it might be stolen.
 
Here’s what to do:
  • Ask the seller for the frame or registration number, so you can check its details on Bike Register
  • Check this number hasn’t been tampered with. You’ll find it somewhere on the bike’s frame
  • Ask the seller to provide a photo ID or signed receipt with their name and address, so you can insure the bike
  • Report to us or the police if you think the bike you’re looking at is stolen. And don’t buy it
 
Here’s our guide for a little more detail:
Tips on buying a bike off Gumtree

        2. Check the bike’s condition
A healthy bike will look good and ride well. It will also be safe, because its previous owners have cared for it.
 
Here’s what to look out for:
  • Check the paintwork is original
  • Make sure there aren’t any big dents
  • Check the tyres aren’t badly worn, and that the wheels spin freely and smoothly
  • Make sure the brakes are tight, chain isn’t damaged, and the gears change smoothly
  • Get the handlebars facing forwards to check the fork (which holds the front wheel) lines up with the frame
  • When you ride the bike, check it isn’t wobbly or shaky
 
Some cyclists like to ride their bikes hard. Ask the seller what they’ve used the bike for, how far they think they’ve cycled, and whether the bike has been in any big accidents.3Register your bike and lock it up well We work closely with law enforcement organisations and cycling groups to help cyclists look after their bikes.
 
      3. Here are our top tips:
  • Use Bike Register to check if a bike is stolen, register your bike, report it stolen and see local bike crime
  • Go to the British Transport Police to learn how to secure your bike, and find local ‘cycle surgeries’ where experts share advice on looking after a bike
  • Check the Metropolitan Police for events where they’ll mark your bike in case it gets stolen
  • Visit the London Cycle Campaign for advice on locking and marking your bike
 
Good luck and safe cycling.

Title: Suspicious Emails
Summary: Our guide on how to recognise fraud emails and which different types of email scams you may see.
Description__c:
In an increasingly online world, it can be hard to know what’s suspicious and what’s not. But there’s no need to be afraid of buying online. Once you know what to look for, scams are often easy to spot. There are two basic types of email scams that it’s important to be able to recognise.

Phishing Emails

Phishing is when fraudsters pretend to be a legitimate person or company to gain access to your information. They are usually looking to get your account login details, financial information, or identification. To learn to identify phishing attempts, read Recognising Phishing and Spoof Attempts.

If you receive a phishing attempt, don’t open any links, download any attachments, or provide any of your information. Contact our customer support team right away to let us know. We will ask you to forward us the email, or a screenshot if it was a pop up on web or mobile. After sending this information to us, delete the email.

Money Scams

Money scams are when fraudsters attempt to convince others to send them money, often in return for something that doesn’t actually exist. This is the most traditional type of scam. Many assume that only buyers are vulnerable to these types of scams, but there are some versions that target sellers.

Although they can come in many forms, they have similar warning signs:

They Move the Conversation to a New Platform

Gumtree has specific security measures in place to try and prevent scam. To avoid these systems, fraudsters will often request that you leave Gumtree and contact them through a private platform. If they ask you to reply to their personal email address instead of their masked Gumtree email, be cautious.

Note: Sometimes these requests can be legitimate, but if they refuse to speak anywhere other than through private email, it might be best to move on. Ask them to speak directly over the phone if they don’t want to use Gumtree messages.

They Can’t Meet In Person

Fraudsters will often work remotely. This is partly because they need to cast a wide net to make money and partly for their own safety. They may have an elaborate excuse that makes them sound legitimate. Some common stories are that they work in an offshore oil rig, that they’re a member of the military, or that they’re buying a special present for a family member from overseas. If a buyer or seller refuses to meet in person, it may be best to move on.

Odd Payment Requests

Since fraudsters don’t usually meet in person, they need the money digitally. They may ask that you send them money through a method with no guarantees. Favourites include MoneyGram, Western Union, and other types of money transfer. They may also request payment through PayPal but insist that you use the Friends & Family setting so that you are offered less protection. They can even create fake PayPal emails. For more information on making safe payments, read our Safe Payments article.

Scams aimed at buyers are generally simple, but there are two types:

  • They ask you to pay for the item before you meet up.
  • They ask for a deposit for an item you haven’t seen.

There are 3 main types of scams aimed at sellers:

  • They insist that you ship the item to them before payment.
  • They send you a payment notification or receipt and ask you to transfer some funds back to them before the full payment comes through.
  • They send you a fake payment notification or receipt, then ask you to transfer some of that money to a shipping company. Not only do they tell you which company to use, but also which account number.

If have reason to suspect that an ad is a scam, don’t proceed any further with the transaction and reach out to our Customer Support team to let us know.

Title: Tips on buying electronic goods
Summary: Our guide on safely buying electronics on Gumtree.
Description__c:
Phones, tablets and other electronics can make great gifts and treats. But be careful when you buy somebody else’s. They’re not always as they seem. Here are our top five tips:
 
       1. Never buy a pre-order item
First, we don’t allow people to list them. So please report anybody trying to sell one. Also, if the seller doesn’t already have the item, you can’t tell if it’s it good enough to buy.
 
       2. Meet the seller face-to-face
That way you can examine the gadget, ask lots of questions and avoid buying something fake, stolen or damaged. If they don’t want to meet, find somebody who does.
 
       3. Ask for a receipt or warranty
If the seller bought the item legitimately, they’ll have these. Or at least be able to tell you why they don’t.
 
        4. Make sure the item works
Check it’s not scratched, broken, locked or hacked.
 
        5. Be careful how you pay
Avoid paying through Western Union, Ukash, MoneyGram, PayPal Family & Friends and PayPal.me. There’s no refund if things go wrong. Normal PayPal is fine though.
 
One final thing: if the item you’re looking for is hard to find or not yet launched, be extra careful. Fraudsters often target these.
 
Good luck in your search, and enjoy your new gadget.

Title: Tips on buying tickets
Summary: Our guide on safely buying tickets on Gumtree.
Description__c:
Seen an event you’d love to go to? It’s best to buy tickets from the event’s website, or an official reseller like StubHub. Especially if it’s a huge event or concert, where fake tickets are more likely.
 
However, if buying from someone else is the only way, follow these tips before you hand over any money:
 
Quiz the seller 
  • Meet the seller face-to-face to make sure the tickets are real. If they live close to you but don’t want to meet, beware. Same if it’s a different person every time you contact them
  • If you’re buying online, make sure the seller already has their hands on the tickets and hasn’t just pre-ordered 
  • Ask for the ticket’s serial number to check with the issuer the ticket hasn’t been bought, reported stolen and refunded. All tickets have serial numbers and bar codes, except those bought on the day from the venue 
  • Ask to see the seller’s receipt and card to make sure they actually bought the ticket the way they say they did
 
Examine the ticket 
  • Check the details on the ticket you’re buying: venue, event date, seat and so on. Are they the same as you saw on the ad? And do they match details on the event’s website? 
  • Make sure the tickets are still valid 
  • Check a card ticket (as opposed to a paper print-out) is real by scratching the front lightly with your fingernail or a coin. If the markings smudge, it’s a fake
 
Check the small print  
  • Are there specific rules? For example, the original buyer needs to be there for you to get in​
  • If an official website says a ticket can’t be resold, don’t buy it. Some events, like Glastonbury, are so strict about reselling, they add the buyer’s photo to the ticket 
  • Make sure the event is still happening, and that you’re old enough to enjoy it
 
Know what to avoid 
  • Avoid e-tickets or tickets already printed out 
  • If tickets are much cheaper than the originals, steer clear. Regardless of the reason the seller gives 
  • Be wary of people who would rather post the tickets than meet you. If you agree to getting the tickets by post, ask for a tracking number and track it 
  • Don’t buy tickets if the seller says you need to pay using another website. Unsecured websites (those that don’t start ‘https’) might steal your money
 
How to buy airline tickets on Gumtree
 
A lot of the information above also applies to buying airline tickets. But here are some more tips:
 
  • First, call the airline and make sure the flight exists 
  • Get all the details you can, including flight number, dates and times, and check they match with the ticket you're looking to buy   
  • Next, very importantly, find the airline’s ticket transfer policy. You might need to pay a fee to change the name on the ticket, for example 
  • If it’s a ticket for a bundle (flight and hotel), check the hotel has proof of the booking. Also, make sure everything you’re expecting – airport transfers, food, spa – is included. There might be a fee for changing the booking into your name
 
To learn more about ticket sales and fraud, read advice from Action Fraud. And for extra tips about online safety, go to Stay Safe Online.
 
If you find the ticket for your event, enjoy the show.  Or if you get the flight you’re after, have a great trip.

If you’re a retailer of everyday items, post what your business offers in Services. Unless you’re advertising small quantities of specific items. See our Rules for Retailers  for more information.

 

Property

 Yes please:

Individuals and agents can post ads for sales, rentals, flat shares, house swaps, holiday homes and homes abroad. 

 

No thanks:

Property is just for advertising properties. If you’re a property agent advertising your business services, you’ll need to post in Services.

 

Jobs

Yes please:
-       Vacancies posted by employers or recruitment agencies

 

Services

 Yes please:
Promote the service your business provides. (This includes retailers selling the kind of everyday items you might find in For Sale.)

Ads for paid-for classes and tuition go here, even when they’re community based.

 

Community

 Yes please:

This is the place to promote free local initiatives and community-level notices – sports clubs, skill swaps, free classes, car pools, events, and lost and found items.

 

No thanks:

 If you’re promoting a local paid-for class, you’re offering a service, so you’ll need to post in Services. You’ll reach the right people in your neighbourhood if you add your precise location.

Pets

 Yes please:

-       Advertise that you want a new home for your pet

-       Sell pet accessories

-       Lost or found a pet? Tell people here.

No thanks:

Wanted ads for pets. There are thousands of pets looking for new homes on Gumtree, and there are thousands of wonderful animals looking for a new start who can be adopted from animal charities. Visit our Pet Advice Hub to find out more.  

Top tip: Still unsure which category is right? Look for ads that are similar to yours and check which category they’re in.

Title: Bike Theft & Scams
Summary: Our guide to buying and selling bicycles safely on Gumtree.
Description__c:
Gumtree is a great place to buy and sell bicycles when you want to save some money. But, like buying or selling anything online, it’s important to proceed carefully and know the warning signs of potential scams.

Buyers

As well as typical scam red flags, there are a few other things to check when buying used bikes.

Inspect the Bike

Like any used item, it’s always a good idea to inspect before buying. Along with looking for a quality frame and tires, check that the brakes a tight, the gears change smoothly, and that it isn’t wobbly or shaky when ridden.

Check Bike Register

Before agreeing to purchase a bike, ask the seller for the frame or registration number. Once you have the number, you can check it on Bike Register. Their site will let you know if the bike has been reported lost or stolen.

Sellers

As well as learning how to accept payments safely, we recommend taking two extra precautions when selling bikes.

Keep Your Bike Secure

Make sure to store your bike in a secure location, preferably inside your home or a locked shed. When locking your bicycle, use two Sold Secure Gold rated locks. Place locks around the frame and both wheels, then secure them to an immovable object.

Register Your Bike

Through the website Bike Register, you can have a serial number printed onto the frame of your bike. This helps the police return your bike to you if it is ever stolen, and will also help to prove to buyers that you are the genuine owner.

Title: Ticket Scams
Summary: Our guide to buying and selling tickets safely.
Description__c:
Gumtree can be a great resource for acquiring tickets to sold-out shows and to helping those who can no longer attend an event. However, like buying or selling anything online, it’s important to proceed carefully and know the warning signs of potential scams. Along with typical scam red flags, there are other things that are especially important to remember when buying tickets.

Avoid E-Tickets

Due to the nature of electronic tickets, they can be very hard to verify when buying second-hand. The ticket files themselves can be duplicated with photo editing software, and it may not be possible to verify that a ticket is authentic until the date of the event. In the interest of community safety, Gumtree has decided to not allow electronic tickets on the site. If someone offers to sell you an electronic ticket, please report the ad to let us know.

Verify the Tickets Whenever Possible

If you can, try to meet the seller at location where the tickets can be verified. For some events, this may be the venue in which they were purchased. Alternatively, you may be able to contact the customer service department of a ticket retailer and request that they check the tickets.

Be Cautious of Bulk Sales or Tickets Far Below Face Value

When people buy tickets to an event, they usually purchase them in groups of one or two. If someone claims to have an unusually high number of tickets, be cautious. Similarly, if the tickets are far cheaper than it would be to buy them from the vendor (especially for sold out events), be extra careful when validating that they’re a genuine seller.

Title: Vehicle Scams
Summary: Our guide to buying and selling vehicles safely on Gumtree.
Description__c:
Gumtree is a great place to buy and sell vehicles. But, like buying or selling anything online, it’s important to proceed carefully. Along with typical scam red flags, there are a few other things that are especially important to be cautious of when buying used vehicles.

Inspect the Vehicle

Like any used item, it’s always a good idea to inspect before buying. You can even ask the seller to meet at a mechanic’s shop and have an inspection done by a professional. If the seller says that you can’t inspect the vehicle for any reason (especially if they claim it’s in a distant location), be cautious.

Test Drive the Vehicle

Test drives are an important part of the car buying experience. However, if at any time you are uncomfortable about the situation, don’t be afraid to walk away.

When test driving a vehicle, make sure to let someone know where you’re going and who the test drive is with. If you can, bring a friend or family member with you.

When selling a vehicle, ask the buyer for their driving license and proof of insurance. If it all checks out, accompany the buyers on the test drive. Let someone else know who you’re driving with and when you’ll be back.

Check the Vehicle History

While Gumtree does do a preliminary history check, it’s best to run another one yourself so that you can see all the details about a vehicle. We recommend the HPI check.

Be Cautious of Escrow Services

Gumtree does not offer escrow services of any kind. If a seller claims that their vehicle is in escrow with us, this is a scam. Do not transfer any money. If they send you invoices or PayPal emails linked to this escrow service, please know that these are not legitimate. Contact us right away if a seller makes these claims.

 

Have more questions about buying a used car? Visit VSTAG for more tips and advice about purchasing a vehicle on Gumtree.

Title: Mobile Phone Scams
Summary: Our guide to buying mobile phones online safely, and how to recognise a potential scam.
Description__c:
Gumtree is a great place to buy and sell used electronics when you want to save some money. But, like buying or selling anything online, it’s important to proceed carefully and know the warning signs of potential scams. Along with typical scam red flags, there are a few other things that are especially important to be cautious of when buying used mobile phones.

Inspect the Phone

Inspections are important for both buyers and sellers, especially with items as complex and delicate as mobile phones. If a seller won’t let you inspect their device (often with the excuse that they’re in a hurry), then it may be best to cancel the deal. Even if the seller believes the phone is in mint condition, double checking is important.

Unlock the Phone

A thorough inspection should include checking things behind the lock screen, like the apps and microphone. Depending on the device you’re buying, the seller may also need to unlink their account before you’ll be able to use it. If they can’t unlock it or refuse to unlock it, it may be best to cancel the transaction.

If you’re selling a phone, remember to wipe your data and private information off of the device before selling it. This will allow the buyer to inspect the device without any risk to your private information.

Check for Claims Against the Phone

If a phone has an insurance claim against it, or is reported lost or stolen, you will not be able to connect it to a network. For a small fee, there are services that will help you check the status of the phone using its IMEI number. We recommend using CheckMEND.

Remember: Take your time and don't rush into any decisions – if in doubt, walk away. You are not obligated to go through with a transaction, even if you’ve already agreed on a price.
