Title: Rehoming a pet
Summary: Our guide to ensuring your beloved pet finds the best possible home through Gumtree.
Description__c:
If it's time to say goodbye to your pet, make sure you send them to the best home possible. They deserve a long and happy life.

The following checklist should help you think about everything you need to ask of a potential new owner. Always read and stick to our posting rules in Getting it Right: Pets. You’ll find specific rehoming advice for your furry, feathered, hairy and scaly friends in our Pet Advice Hub. 

Quiz the potential new owners
Every animal has different needs. From exercise to food, health and companionship, does the potential new owner have the knowledge and lifestyle to match what your animal needs?

You know your pet best, so ask lots of questions and pay attention to the person’s questions and reactions. If they don't seem interested in the health and happiness of your animal, wait for the right person who’ll give them the love and attention they deserve.  

Do they understand the commitment?
Some animals, like birds, horses or exotics, can live for a long time and require time-consuming daily care. If you’re at all unsure that the potential new owner doesn’t grasp the commitment, wait for someone who does.

Share as much knowledge as possible
Does your pet become aggressive? Need specialist care? Grow very large? Live for a long time? Require a licence or paperwork to be legally kept or sold? Make sure the person looking to buy knows this.

Check it's not an impulse buy
People who spontaneously buy an animal, especially an exotic, usually haven't done their homework. If you think this is the case, make sure the potential owner understands your animal. Exotic pets often end up with animal charities after people realise they're not easy to care for or the novelty wears off.

Ask your vet
If you need more advice about selling your pet, speak to your local vet. They can help you with medical history certificates, talk to you about neutering, vaccinating, microchipping, and lots more.

Make sure your animals are old enough
Puppies and kittens need to be at least eight weeks, ideally 12 weeks, old before they leave their mother.

Get the paperwork ready
When you find the perfect new owner, remember to hand over all the documents they'll need, like vet records medical history, vaccination certificates, and records of worming and flea treatment. Make sure any registration papers, hereditary disease screening certificates and microchip documentation are in order.

Meet the family
Try to have all members of the potential new family meet your pet. This way you'll have peace of mind that your friend is a good fit.

You can say no
Agreeing to a viewing doesn’t mean you have to give your pet to the first person who shows an interest. Say no if you have concerns.

Consider doing it offline
An animal welfare organisation might be the best option for your pet’s long-term health and wellbeing. If you do decide to post an ad with us, be honest about their needs and behaviour in your ad description.

Title: Safety at the Meet Up
Summary: Our guide to having a successful, safe transaction in person.
Description__c:
Once you’ve come to an agreement and decided you’re going to make the trade, it’s important to meet in person. Meeting in person helps to prevent miscommunication, allows you to inspect the item one last time, and reduces the risk of scams.

Agree on a Safe Location

Unless you’re selling an item that can’t be moved easily, it’s best to meet somewhere other than your own home. A public location will help ensure safety for both parties, especially if you can’t meet until the evening. Try to choose somewhere with plenty of light, other people, and if possible, security cameras. Meeting in coffee shops, fast food restaurants, or even the parking lot of police stations are good choices.

Bring a Friend

Bringing a friend or family member with you is always a good idea. They can keep you company while you’re waiting and help ensure everything goes smoothly.

Inspect What You're Buying Carefully

Even if you’ve seen photos and the seller ensures you that it’s in perfect condition, it’s important to inspect the item thoroughly first. Even genuine sellers may not notice small stains, cracks, or other issues. If you’re buying a vehicle, taking the vehicle to a mechanic together to have it inspected can settle any final concerns.

The inspection is equally important for a seller. Ensure that the buyer looks over the item, turns it on, and knows about any wear and tear beforehand. That last inspection will make sure that both you and the buyer are aware of the items condition. This step will ensure that nothing is left unsaid that could cause issues later.

Once you’ve agreed to the deal, it’s time to complete the payment. Continue reading about safe payments.

Title: Staying Safe in Jobs
Summary: Our guide to help you stay safe in the Jobs category.
Description__c:
The best advice we can give when looking for or advertising a new role is to follow our Getting it Right Guide, avoid discrimination pitfalls and follow the SAFERjobs guidelines published here : - https://www.safer-jobs.com/advice.cfm

If someone’s reluctant to play by these rules when you’re negotiating, walk away. And please, always report suspicious behaviour.

Meet face to face and tell others when and where you’re going
meet in daylight if you can. Choose somewhere busy, like your local coffee shop. If you need to meet at a house, always have a friend with you.

Never send payment for items you haven’t seen
The safest way to buy is to see and check what you’re getting before you pay for it.

If an ad or reply sounds too good to be true, it probably is
Everyone likes a bargain, but do your research and know the fair market value for the item. Ask lots of questions and request paperwork, certificates and receipts. Search your seller’s number or business online to check if they have any history or reviews.

Use the ‘Reply to ad’ button for your safety and privacy
Always keep your communications within Gumtree. Anyone who tries to lure you away from our site is probably trying to avoid our filter system that stops spam and suspicious emails.

Beware of fake Gumtree, eBay or escrow websites and emails
We’ll never ask you for login, password, bank or credit card details over email or text. If anyone does, report it. Also, visit and check websites directly, never through a link you’ve been sent.

Don’t carry large sums of money when meeting up
If you want to buy an item, agree a price in advance and only take that amount. Sellers can check bank notes are genuine before accepting them with our Gumtree guide to spotting fake cash.

Avoid shipping when possible
But if face-to-face really isn’t possible, stick to the following rules:

-       Agree any postage costs when you agree the price
-       If you’re the buyer, you shouldn’t have to pay unexpected fees for brokerage or import duties
-       Confirm when you’re received the item, and expect the seller to confirm payment

Don’t use Paysafe, Ukash or Western Union for Gumtree trades
Certain payment methods give you a level of protection. But these don’t. Be suspicious of a seller who asks you to switch payment method (usually from a safer one like PayPal), claiming they have account issues. Use our guide to get familiar with paying online.

Title: What Information Can Be Seen When I Post?
Summary: Our guide to keeping your information private when you post on Gumtree.
Description__c:
In this day and age, privacy is on everyone’s mind. Gumtree protects your privacy by giving you complete control over what information other users can see. Below, we’ll explain how to work with the security measures that Gumtree has in place to keep you safe.

Emails and Phone Numbers

By default, Gumtree masks your email and hides your phone number behind the Reveal button. It can be tempting to include contact information in the body of your ad to speed up communication. However, by putting this information in the description you’re side-stepping the protections we’ve put in place to protect your information. This can increase the chance that you’ll be contacted by those who would otherwise not be able to get around our security measures.

Name

The name in your Profile is the name that will appear on your ads. It’s safest to use your first name only, or even a nickname. Including your last name is not required or recommended.

Address

When you post an ad on Gumtree, you can select a city or type in your postal code. Whichever you choose, you will have the option to include a map that will show a point over the centre of your city or postal code. If you don’t want other users to see your postal code, you can always remove it by unchecking ‘Show a map on my ad’ from the post or edit ad page.

Giving out your street address shouldn’t be necessary in most cases. We recommend meeting at a safe third-party location whenever possible. If you are selling something that cannot be easily moved, it’s best to only provide your address once you’ve agreed to make the deal or arranged an inspection. Posting your address in the ad description is not recommended.

Title: Posting Ads in Jobs
Summary: Our guide to posting ads on Gumtree Jobs.
Description__c:
Posting ads on Gumtree Jobs is as easy as posting a normal ad on Gumtree. Simply follow the steps below:

  1. Click Post a job ad at the top of the Gumtree Jobs page.
  2. Read the “advertise your job today” section, then click Post your job.
  3. Fill in the details of the job opening. For more information about each field, click into the field itself. A bubble will appear with information about that field.
  4. Choose where to categorise your ad using the drop-down lists. These options will control what search filters your ad appears under when job seekers are looking through the site.
  5. Upload a logo (optional). Adding a logo to your ad is free, but it will only appear after a job seeker opens your ad. To have your logo appear on the search results page for a small fee, click the check box underneath.
  6. Choose a contact type. By default, applications to your ad will be sent to the email you used to register for Gumtree. If you’d prefer a different contact method, click on “Or select a different contact type”. Choose your contact method and include your new email/website (if needed). If you’d like to also be contacted by phone, include a phone number.
  7. If you’d like to apply a feature to your ad, click on the box beside that feature. We offer 5 types of features that can help to draw attention to your ad.
  8. Choose when your ad goes live or is taken down. The posting date defaults to the current day, but you can alter this by clicking Edit Dates. Under From, choose the day, month, year in the first box. The hour (second box) and the minute (third box) are optional. Choose a To date that is 60 days or less from your posting date. You cannot exceed the 60-day runtime.
  9. Once you’re satisfied with your ad, click Save and continue.
  10. If you have more ads you need to post, click +Add another job to create a new ad. Once you’ve created all of the ads you want to post, click Continue to Payment.

Once your payment is submitted, your ad will be processed. Processing times can vary depending on how busy Gumtree Jobs is at the time. If it's taking a little longer than excepted, please bear with us. Once it goes live we’ll send you an email to confirm, and a link to your ad.

  • Follow the payment instructions and click Purchase.

Title: How do I create a great ad in For Sale?
Summary: Our guide to posting effective ads in For Sale.
Description__c:
It is easy to post an ad online quickly, but to maximise your effort consider the many ways your ad might be improved to catch a buyer’s attention. There are many factors to creating an effective classified ad. Here are a few tips from our experts:

 

Create Titles that Attract

Gumtree’s search function uses the keywords included in the title of your ad. To make sure that your ad appears for as many buyers as possible, make sure that you use detailed, specific keywords. Gumtree allows up to 100 characters; don’t be afraid to use them all!

Example: The title “Sofa for sale” may be accurate but it won’t return a lot of results. Try adding more detail: “Incredibly comfortable, 3-seater sofa for sale. Red Fabric. Barely used, still in great condition.”

 

Add Detailed Photos

Ads with photos receive higher quality, more serious replies than those without. Adding well lit, good quality images to your ad will go a long way in creating buyer interest. There is no cost to post a picture on Gumtree, so take advantage and include multiple images in your ads.

 

Choose the Category Carefully

It is important to ensure that you post your ad to the correct city and category. If your ad is miscategorised, interested buyers may have a difficult time locating it. Double check where ads like yours are categorised and try posting in that category. After checking your category, double check the city your ad is posted in. If locals can’t see it, it will negatively affect your number of responses.

 

Compare Your Price

One of the most common mistakes that new sellers make is listing their items at too high a price. If your item is used, buyers expect a bit of a deal. Look for similar ads on the site to see how other sellers are listing their items. Comparing your price to others should help you gauge the range you want to be within.

 

Promote Your Ads

Sometimes, an ad might need a little boost to receive the exposure it deserves. Free classifieds are a great start, but if you are motivated towards increasing exposure, consider upgrading your free advertisement with a paid feature.

Title: Getting it Right: Posting in For Sale
Summary: Our guide to posting great ads in the For Sale category.
Description__c:
Gumtree is the #1 classifieds site in the UK. That means a lot of footfall. Great. But with so many people using our site, it also means you need to be careful. If you’re a private seller or a retailer, follow these common sense posting rules for happy trading.
 

Understanding the basics

Before posting anything, check our A-Z of items you can't buy or sell on Gumtree . If you try to advertise something from this list and have paid for your ad, you won’t get a refund when we have to remove it. Also:

-       No duplicates please
Don’t create more than one ad for the same item, or create multiple accounts.

-       Don’t leave it live
Once your ad has done its job, delete it. If you don’t, other users might still contact you about it, which is a nuisance for them and you.

-       If it’s not in your possession, don’t try to sell it
This includes tickets and pre-order items. Check our special guidelines for selling tickets as it can be more complex than you might imagine. Be careful not to show ticket barcodes in your photos, especially with e-tickets as someone could copy and use them.

Also, you can only sell items based in the UK.

Putting everything in the right place

-       Get the category right
Our categories work hard to connect the right ad with the right buyer. Please don’t try to get  more views or avoid paying our fees by posting in the wrong one. You’ll get better results when your ad appears in the right place.

When you create your ad, the template makes it easy with category and sub-category suggestions. But For Sale is a big category. If you're looking for Freebies, Stuff Wanted or Swap Shop, just keep scrolling through the list. 

-       Follow the ad template
Keep website links and contact details in the designated place and out of your ad title, description and photos.

-       Got a job lot?
It’s free to post as many ads in For Sale as you like. So only post multiple items in one ad if you’re selling them as a job lot.

The same applies to trade sellers, but you’ll need to pay a fee of £2 per ad. Trade sellers must also stick to our Rules for Retailers

Creating an ad that works

 -       Use plain English and keep it clean. That goes for the images you post too. You’re welcome to add a translation in another language in your item description.

-       Steer clear of disputes by writing a clear and honest description of your item. Don't be tempted to add any keyword spamming.

-       Make sure the price is right. Clearly state the price you want for your item. You’re welcome to invite near offers, but not bids. Gumtree isn’t an auction house.

-       Aim for face-to-face. Don’t say you’ll only send an item in the post. Gumtree is a community. We encourage our users to meet face-to-face whenever possible.

Title: Getting it Right: Posting in Jobs
Summary: Our guide to posting great ads in the Jobs category.
Description__c:
Gumtree Jobs is the gateway to over 100,000 full-time and part-time vacancies across the UK – from apple picking to yacht building. Posting in Jobs requires you to stay within the law, as well as within the following posting rules.

Make sure your ad doesn’t discriminate based on age, disability, gender, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation. Equal treatment in access to employment is protected by law.

Plus, jobs must offer the National Minimum Wage or above.

Understanding the basics 

-      No duplicates please
Don’t create more than one ad for one vacancy, or create multiple accounts. Though you can post your ad in more than one geographic location if you need to advertise to neighbouring areas.

-       Under 18?
It’s 18 and over here, please.

 Putting everything in the right place

Although you’ll find thousands of jobs on Gumtree, we’re not the right place for everything. Check the list below for jobs you can’t advertise here. And remember: if you offer something on this list, you won’t get a refund when we remove your ad.

-      Escort or adult industry work, including glamour or webcam modelling
-      Clinical/medical trials
-      Some work-from-home jobs
-      Pyramid selling schemes.

If you’re posting on behalf of a direct selling enterprise, such as Avon or Herbalife, don’t post as a private individual. You’ll need to contact us and upgrade to a business account

-       Get the category right
Our categories work hard to connect the right ad with the right job hunter. Please don’t try to get more views or avoid paying our fees by posting in the wrong one. You’ll get better results when your ad appears in the right place.

-       Follow the ad template
Keep website links and contact details in the designated place and out of your ad title, description and photos.

Writing a great ad

-       Use plain English and keep it clean. That goes for the images you post too. You’re welcome to add a translation in another language in your item description.
-       Be clear. To attract the best candidates, write a clear and honest description of your vacancy. Don’t be tempted to spam with keywords. The ads that get the best response are the ones that say clearly what the job involves.

Be especially clear what your vacancy involves if your industry has an adult services sector, such as modelling or massage.

Be professional

-      If you’re a recruitment agency, say so.
-      In certain sectors, you must have a landline phone number in your contact details. These include charity and voluntary sector recruiters, and modelling agencies.

Title: Getting it Right: Posting in Motors
Summary: Our guide to posting great ads in the Motors category.
Description__c:
Buying and selling vehicles can be fun and stress-free when everyone deals honestly and clearly.

It’s our aim to make that happen and keep everyone safe online. We’ve created the following guidance to help you become the ideal private seller or business trader.

Understanding the basics

-       No duplicates please
Don’t create more than one ad for the same car, or create multiple accounts.

-       Don’t leave it live
Once your ad has done its job, delete it. If you don’t, other users might still contact you about it, which is a nuisance for them and you.

-       Private sellers get one free ad at a time
You can have a maximum of two live Motor ads at a time. It’s £17.99 for your second ad.

-       Is it parked outside?
If you don’t have the vehicle you’re selling in your possession, or it’s not in the UK, Gumtree isn’t the way to sell it.

Putting everything in the right place  

-       Get the category right
Our categories work hard to connect the right ad with the right buyer. Please don’t try to get  more views or avoid paying our fees by posting in the wrong one. You’ll get better results when your ad appears in the right place.
If your vehicle isn’t fit for the road, post it in the relevant Parts or Accessories category instead.

-       Follow the ad template
Keep website links and contact details in the designated place and out of your ad title, description and photos. Don't be tempted to spam with keywords.

 Creating an ad that works 

-       Steer clear of disputes
Write a clear and honest description of your vehicle. When your ad is fair and accurate, your car should be revving off to its new home in no time.

-       The price is right

-       Enter important details with care
Our site gathers information from your vehicle registration number (VRN). If you add an incorrect VRN, we may delete your ad. (The VRN won’t be displayed on your ad, unless you include it in your photos.)

Extra guidance for our trade users

One more thing. We have absolutely nothing to do with the browser extension ‘Freethetree’ and don’t allow you to use it.

Title: Getting it right: Posting in Pets
Summary: Our guide to posting great ads in the Pets category.
Description__c:
Animal welfare is our number one priority in our Pets category. Our goal is that all animals advertised for sale online are advertised legally and ethically.

We rely on you doing everything you can to check your furry (or scaly) friend is going to a responsible home. Our Rehoming Guides are packed with information that will help.

Here’s an overview of our top posting rules.

Be honest

-       Your pet has the best chance of finding its happy forever home if you give the new owners all the information they need. Don’t withhold something that could cause problems for them (and your pet) down the line. 
-       You can only post your ad if it has a photo. Use recent photos that give a good likeness – no stock photos please. And if you’re advertising a whole litter, post a photo of that litter.
-       Get the birth date right so that the advertised rehoming date is right. No young animal should be removed from its mother too soon.   

 

A pet is for life… 

-       Never suggest buying an animal as a gift
-       Don’t use gimmicky photos – a picture of your dog looking cute in a handbag isn’t the right reason for someone to take him or her on
-       If your pet is good with children, say so. But never say a pet is good ‘for’ children.
-       If a new owner is persuaded by an ad to take on a pet without considering the long-term commitment needed, it’s unlikely to be in the animal’s best interests. Always act in a way that encourages respect for our furry friends.

Help us prevent animal cruelty

We don’t allow the sale of certain animals. When you’re creating your ad, if there isn’t a category for your pet, you can’t sell or rehome it on Gumtree.

Also, you can’t advertise animals with cropped ears, docked tails, or clipped wings on Gumtree. And if you’re rehoming a rescue animal, contact a sanctuary or charity instead.

-       Never sell a pregnant animal or advertise a pet as being suitable for breeding.
-       No more than two pets or litters per year, please.
-       Collect or deliver in person. Never send an animal in the post.
-       Be vigilant: if you see a puppy advertised as having a pet passport and under 15 weeks, please report the ad to Gumtree. Puppies do not come with a passport if they’ve been bred in the UK, so the only reason a puppy would need one is if it has been imported.

And remember – you have no obligation to sell to the first person who responds. Familiarise yourself with the tips in our Rehoming Guides. Your pet may find a better home if you advertise through a local charity or sanctuary instead. Please do what’s right for them.  Moreover, we only allow 2 litters every 12 months and all pets need to be at least 8 week old in order for them to be sold on Gumtree.

Looking for a Pets Wanted category?  

If you’re looking to welcome a new pet into your family, there are hundreds to choose from on Gumtree. Or you might consider offering a new start to one of the thousands of wonderful animals in rescue centres across the UK. For this reason, we don’t have a Pets Wanted category.

Make sure you read our Buyers Guide to help you take the right steps.

Title: Tips on buying your dream home
Summary: Our guide to safely buying property on Gumtree.
Description__c:
Taking that first step onto the property ladder can be as nail-biting as it is exciting. Follow our tips to help you find your dream home:
 
1.  Do your research 
  • Visit the neighbourhoods where you’d like to live. What’s important to you? Good transport links? Local shops? A good pub? 
  • Ask locals about the area. What are its good and bad points? 
  • Check planning websites to see if any large developments are on the horizon 
  • Check environmental agency websites for flood risk areas
 
2.  View some properties 
  • Take a friend when you view a property. It’s safer and you’ll also have a second opinion 
  • Ask if you can take photos so you can review pros and cons later 
  • Ask the estate agent or vendor lots of questions. How old is the boiler? Has the roof been checked recently? How old are the windows? When was it last rewired? Is parking an issue? The more the better
  • View properties at different times of the day. Look for potential on-street parking issues, noisy neighbours or loud pubs and restaurants 
  • Look out for damp, mould and cracks. Check that windows and doors open and close easily. Look at woodwork, and check that the roof looks in good health 
  • Do a second viewing if you’re unsure about anything 
 
3.  Keep on top of the law and money
 
  • Only use an accredited solicitor or legal representative. Ask friends for recommendations 
  • Get your legal representative to check all paperwork and documents relating to the sale of the property, including proof of ownership 
  • Get a survey carried out 
  • Never hand over money to estate agents or vendors before, during or after viewing a property 
  • Don’t feel under pressure to complete a transaction 
  • Ask your solicitor to check that all financial transactions are legal and carried out the right way
 Keep in mind that at Gumtree we never get involved in payment processes. So, make sure you have a good team around you.
 
The leasehold option

Many flats are sold as ‘leasehold’. This means you’ll own the property for a fixed amount of time. Your lease will tell you how long. When the lease runs out, the property returns to the freeholder. If you’re buying leasehold:
 
  • Check the number of years left on a lease. Most mortgage companies won’t lend on short leases
  • Are there less than 85 years left on the lease? Look at the cost and legal implications of extending the lease
  • Ask about any ground rent and service charges you might need to pay. These can add up
  • Find out who owns the freehold
  • Find out if you get a share of the freehold
  • Seek specialist legal advice 
 
As always, if something seems too good to be true, it probably is. If you’re unsure or want any extra advice, you can speak with the Citizens Advice Bureau. 
 
Take time to settle in to your new home. And enjoy it.

Title: Tips on renting a holiday home
Summary: Our guide to safely renting a holiday home on Gumtree.
Description__c:
Planning and booking a holiday can be a fun experience. As long as you steer clear of any scams out there. Here are our top tips for a stress-free holiday rental experience:
 
Planning your break 
  • Ask family, friends and colleagues for recommendations
  • Check online reviews to see what other people say about the flat, house, holiday park or caravan you’ve seen 
Booking your getaway 
  • Compare like-for-like rental prices in your chosen area. Are you paying more than the going rate? Is there a reason?
  • If your holiday home is much cheaper than similar rentals, again ask yourself why. Is it miles from tourist attractions? No parking or wifi?
  • Call the owner to check details and ask questions about the local area. Check their Facebook page or website. Are descriptions and photos consistent?
  • If you’re renting a caravan on a holiday park, check the caravan owner’s details with the park’s managers
  • Look at online maps to check the location of your holiday rental. Use ‘street view’ if it’s available, and check that images match what you’re expecting
  • Ask extra questions if you want more details. Reputable owners and agencies are always happy to help
 
Be aware that when you rent directly from an owner, the price is usually slightly lower.
 
Being security conscious 
  • Use secure payment methods for deposits, balances and damage deposits. And always get somebody to email or text you proof of payment
  • Read through any damage deposit policy very carefully
  • Ask for a confirmation of your booking by text or email 
  • Take the owner’s or agency’s contact details with you on holiday (full name, number, email address) along with the details and address of your rental
  • Think about taking out travel insurance. You’ll usually be covered for cancellation, medical expenses, lost luggage and other losses. Again, read your policy very carefully
 
Always use your common sense and best judgement. If something feels not quite right, look again for your perfect holiday rental.
 
Enjoy your holiday.

Title: Suspicious Ads
Summary: Our guide to spotting ads that may be fraud, scams, or otherwise not genuine.
Description__c:
Most ads on Gumtree are posted by genuine sellers. When someone with bad intentions does come through the site, we have systems in place to try to catch them before any damage can be done. Despite these protections, any time you are buying or selling online it’s important to know how to recognise suspicious ads. There are a few warning signs to watch out for.

Too Good to be True Deals

In order to try and lure people into their scam, fraudsters will offer a deal that’s hard to refuse. They are likely to offer new or popular items at a fraction of the cost of similar ads. The advert may explain that the item is practically new, has all the best features, and has never had any issues. If any item, property, or vehicle seems to be too good a deal, be cautious.

If you’re the one selling the item, they may offer you more than asking price, or may want to buy everything you have for sale all at once.

Stock Photos

In most cases, fraudsters don’t actually have the item or property they’re offering. Instead, they pull photos from online. They often choose the best quality photos that are the most likely to convince you to buy. One quick method to check if the photos are genuine is to do a quick image search.

Note: While stock images can be a bad sign, they don’t necessarily mean an ad is a scam. Genuine sellers do sometimes use images from online, especially if the item is new. Don’t worry unless you see other red flags as well. If you’re unsure, you can always request original photos.

Email in Their Ad

Fraudsters will often request that you leave Gumtree and contact them through a private platform. This helps them to avoid our security systems. If they ask you to reply to their personal email address instead of their masked Gumtree email, be cautious.

Tip: If for some reason a seller doesn’t want to use Gumtree messages to communicate, ask to give them a call. Fraudsters will rarely speak directly over the phone.

For more information about suspicious activity after contacting a seller, read our Safety in Messages article.

Title: Avoiding Scammers
Summary: Our guide to spotting phishing scams and keeping your information safe.
Description__c:
Technology now plays a big part in all of our lives. Most of the time it’s a positive, but occasionally fraudsters use it to try to scam others through a method known as ‘phishing’.

What’s phishing?

Phishing is when somebody emails, texts or calls another person pretending to be a reputable company. In reality, they’re a scammer and they’re trying to steal personal details. They're often after passwords, banking information, or personal identification.

What does phishing look like?

Fraudsters go to great lengths to mimic real companies. They can use logos, similar email addresses and even the names of employees to appear more realistic. Learning to spot phishing attempts comes down to recognizing when you are dealing with the real organization, and when it may be a fake. Below are a few telling signs that it's a phishing attempt.

Signs of phishing websites:

  • Alarmist or exciting statements. In order to get others to act quickly, they'll often claim that you must login or make a payment quickly before your ad is deleted or account closed. Alternatively, they may claim that you've won a contest that you haven't entered. Legitimate companies don’t do this.
  • Asking immediately for personal information. Phishing sites will bring up a web form asking for your personal information right away. Don’t confirm card details, account names or passwords unless you’re sure it’s the real website. Gumtree pages will always be on www.gumtree.com or my.gumtree.com. Look for the padlock in the address bar before you enter your details. If you’re not sure, don’t share. Tip: If you're really not sure it's the real site, close the link and find the company's website through a google search. It should look the same. 
  • Small details don't seem right. Phishing websites are often made in a hurry, so they'll miss small details like spelling mistakes, name changes and proper formatting. 
  • The site is blocked by your web browser or anti-virus software. Fake websites often contain malicious software (malware). It lets scammers tamper with your computer and sometimes steal personal information.

Signs of phishing emails:

  • Alarmist or exciting statements. In order to get others to act quickly, they'll often claim that you must login or make a payment quickly before your ad is deleted or account closed. Alternatively, they may claim that you've won a contest that you haven't entered. Legitimate companies don’t do this.
  • Non-specific names. Real companies will almost always address you by the name you used to register for their site. If an email starts off with a generic introduction like "Dear User" or "Dear Gumtree Customer", while also asking for your immediate action, be cautious.
  • Bad spelling and grammar. Many phishing attempts come from overseas, and often use odd phrasing, incorrect spelling or bad grammar.
  • Odd email addresses. They’ll often look a bit different to the real thing, or contain mistakes. An email from xxxx@gumtree.com doesn't prove that it’s from us.
  • Requesting your pins or passwords. If they're trying to gain access to your Gumtree account, they may ask that you provide your password within the email. Gumtree will never ask for your password in an email. If they're trying to gain access to banking details, they'll ask you to provide your bank name or account number with a PIN or your account password via email. Banks don’t operate like this.

Signs of phishing phone calls:

  • Asking to confirm your account details. Fraudsters will call you out of the blue and ask you to confirm personal details, passwords or bank details. Legitimate companies won’t do this.
  • Instructions to login to a very specific site. Rather than just telling you to go onto their site by the usual method, they'll provide instructions to visit and log into ‘your’ account immediately. Details will usually lead to a fake website.
  • Immediate payment requests. People who ask you to pay for something over the phone. Don’t share any of your bank or card details.
  • Automated messages asking you to call back. Fraudsters will often use automated calls or messages where you’re asked to call a specific number back. These are often on 084, 087 or 09 numbers and you could be kept on hold to run up a large bill. Don’t call back.

Signs of phishing text messages:

  • Asking to confirm your account details. Fraudsters will text you out of the blue and ask you to confirm personal details, passwords or bank details. Legitimate companies won’t do this. If you get one, forward it to your network provider using 7726, or delete it.
  • Suspicious links within the text. Fraudsters will often send phishing websites through text. If you don't recognize the URL or it looks suspicious, don't click it. If it's a legitimate text from a company, you should still be able to access any promotions or information if you visit their site independently of the link in a text. 
  • Strange-looking replies to ‘for sale’ ads. These are another way to fool you into clicking on fake links or replying to fake email addresses.
  • Alarmist or exciting statements. In order to get others to act quickly, they'll often claim that you must login or make a payment quickly before your ad is deleted or account closed. Alternatively, they may claim that you've won a contest that you haven't entered. Legitimate companies don’t do this.
  • Non-specific names. Real companies will almost always address you by the name you used to register for their site. If an email starts off with a generic introduction like "Dear User" or "Dear Gumtree Customer", while also asking for your immediate action, be cautious.
  • Bad spelling and grammar. Many phishing attempts come from overseas, and often use odd phrasing, incorrect spelling or bad grammar.

What should I do if I receive a phishing attempt?

  • Never follow the links and don’t share personal information. Always go to websites directly, using your browser. If in doubt, call the company or bank to find out what’s going on.
  • Report the phishing attempt through Action Fraud's website. 

How can I protect myself?

  • Protect your computer with the latest version of your web browser and use an anti-virus program.
  • Never let your email address or passwords be publicly visible on any website.
  • Always check contact numbers and websites independently.
  • Hang up on suspicious callers.
  • Don’t open suspicious links or websites.
  • Don’t respond to suspicious texts or emails. You can forward texts to your network provider using 7726, or just delete them.
  • If you’re suspicious of a business that’s been in touch, contact them directly to check it was them.
  • Don’t pay anything if you’re told you’ve won a prize or competition.
  • Look for spelling and grammar mistakes in emails, texts and on websites.
  • Look for inaccurate brand names or company logos.
  • Check the internet for information on the latest scams. There are often online warnings, and police websites carry up-to-date information.
  • Trust your instincts. If it doesn’t ‘feel right’, it probably isn’t.
  • If you have doubts but aren't sure, check your suspicions with friends and family.

How do I know if a Gumtree email is genuine?

  • Emails from Gumtree will be sent from mail@info.gumtree.com, reply@info.gumtree.com, noreply@gumtree.com, or email@Gumtreejobs.com. If it's from another Gumtree member, will be sent through our masked email system and will end in @reply.gumtree.com. 
  • We don’t get involved in payments or item delivery between buyers and sellers. Be very wary if someone contacts you pretending to be us and trying to get involved.
  • We won't ask for your account password, banking details, or any other potentially sensitive information over email. If you receive an email that looks like it's from us requesting this information, don't click any links in the email.

Title: Recognising Phishing and Spoof Attempts
Summary: Our guide to spotting suspicious emails and identifying phishing emails and spoof sites.
Description__c:
In order to protect the security of your account, it’s important to be able to recognise phishing attempts and spoof sites. Phishing is a term used when fraudsters try to gain access to personal account logins. Spoofs are websites or emails that attempt to mimic a particular company in order to trick users into providing their information. Most phishing attempts come in the form of spoof sites or emails.

Spotting a Phishing Attempt

Fraudsters go to great lengths to mimic real companies. They can use logos, similar email addresses, and even the names of employees to appear more realistic. Learning to spot phishing attempts comes down to recognising when you are dealing with the true organisation, and when it may be a spoof. Here a few key signs to watch out for:

Alarmist statements

In an attempt to get users to act quickly, fraudsters often start messages with urgent claims such as ‘Your Account has been disabled. Change your password now to regain access or it will be deleted.’ These can also be positive statements, such as ‘You’ve qualified for a discount! Confirm your account information now to receive free features!’

Asking for confidential Information

In order to gain access to your accounts, fraudsters ask for passwords, bank accounts, or credit card information. Our team will never request this type of personal account information over email. We will also never send password reset emails unless you’ve specifically requested one through the ‘Forgot your password?’ button on the Gumtree login page.

Bad Spelling and Grammar

Many phishing attempts come from overseas, and often use odd phrasing, incorrect spelling or bad grammar.

Suspicious Email Addresses

Legitimate Gumtree emails will come from @info.gumtree.com or @gumtree.com email addresses. Don’t be fooled by emails such as gumtreesupport@hotmail.com or security@gumtree.support.com

Spotting a Spoof Site

Whenever you are asked to enter in your password, double check the URL of the page. It should read as https://my.gumtree.com/login. If you don’t see the S in https:// or if there is anything between gumtree.com and the first forward slash (Ex. gumtree.com.spoof.com/), don’t click. Many browsers also have a secure connection symbol that will appear next to the URL as a small lock icon. Here’s what a secure URL looks like in the Chrome browser:

When asked to use a link within an email you can hover over it before clicking to see the true URL. Depending on what browser or email application you’re using, you may see this at the bottom of your window, or as a pop up next to your curser. If it looks suspicious, don’t click.

What to Do

If you receive a phishing attempt, don’t open any links, download any attachments, or provide any of your information. 

Report this attempt to:

  • https://safebrowsing.google.com/safebrowsing/report_phish
  • https://report.netcraft.com/report
  • report@phishing.gov.uk
  • direct to your email service provider
  • direct to our customer service team.

When you report this please include a copy of the email, a screen shot of the site and the spoof site URL. If escalated to our Customer Service Team we will forward this information to our specialised team to have the site shut down.

We will then forward the information you provide to our specialised teams to have the spoof site shut down.

Title: Safe Payments
Summary: Our guide to transferring payments safely while buying or selling.
Description__c:
Once you’ve met, inspected the item and come to an agreement, it’s time to finalise the deal. There are many options to transfer money, both online and in person. Let’s take a look at the benefits of each.

Deposits

Requesting or offering deposits for items on Gumtree is not recommended. However, some sellers do request one. Never pay a deposit on an item you haven’t seen in person. If you have seen it and you’re not completely comfortable leaving a deposit, it may be best to move on to another deal.

Cash

Cash is often the safest option. It’s generally accepted by everyone and is very hard to fake convincingly. However, it’s not impossible. If you’re accepting cash, especially for a large purchase, make sure you know how to recognize counterfeit currency.

Carrying cash as a buyer can have its own risks and be less convenient. Consider the situation and decide what’s best for you.

Cheque

Cheques can be more convenient than cash, but they can bounce. If you want a cheque, the safest option is to ask for a certified cheque and go to the bank with them to cash it before the item is signed over.

PayPal

When used cautiously, PayPal is a great tool for sending and receiving money online. When accepting a PayPal payment, always double check that the payment has actually been deposited into your account. PayPal payment confirmation emails can be faked, so make sure to check independently of the email (without using any links). If the payment confirmation email claims the payment won’t appear in your account for any reason, contact PayPal (directly through their website, not the email) before proceeding.

PayPal has some protections in place to help both buyers and sellers, but these protections don’t extend to all PayPal transactions. We do not recommend using PayPal’s Friends and Family payment option, as this skips their internal security and doesn’t offer protection.

If you’re ever not sure about a PayPal transfer, you can contact PayPal directly for help verifying it. Learn more about fake PayPal emails.

Money Wiring Services such as Western Union/MoneyGram

We do not recommend using direct money transfers services such as Western Union or MoneyGram. Electronic transfers are hard to verify because payment confirmation emails can be faked by fraudsters. Should the deal fall though, or if it turns out to be scam, they offer no protection. If you decide to accept payment through one of these methods, don’t give them the item until you’ve been able to confirm with 100% certainty that the funds are in your account.

Note: If any buyer sends you an electronic transfer and then asks you to move some of the funds somewhere else – especially if they require the funds to be moved before you actually receive the money – don’t do it. This is likely an SMS scam. If you encounter any requests like this, please report it to our customer support team.

Bank Transfers

Like money wiring services, bank transfers may appear to offer a safe way to transfer money between a buyer and seller. However, once you have sent funds they are almost immediately transferred into the account of the recipient. If a deal was to fall through, or you were unhappy with the item you had paid for, your money is not protected. Transfers offer few options for a refund beyond the good will of the seller. We always urge caution when transferring money by bank. We recommend that you are completely satisfied with the item before committing to the transaction.

Fake Banking Apps

As scammers get more sophisticated, their methods can get harder to spot. Fake banking and payment apps are services that appear to be genuine, but in fact are ways for buyers to make it appear that money has been transferred to a sellers account, when it hasn't. If you are going to use a banking or payment service to receive funds, please follow this advice:

  • Do not feel pressured into using banking or payment app to receive funds
  • Insist on using a service you are familiar with and only use the app that you already have installed and verified on your phone or device
  • Never had over goods without having received the money; double check your banking app to ensure the funds are present in your account
  • Be wary of users who say funds are pending - if the buyer says funds will appear in a few hours or a few days, this should be a red flag

Title: Scammers Recruiting Others
Summary: Our guide to understanding and avoiding recruitment scams.
Description__c:
Gumtree has many protections and processes in place to stop fraud attempts before they ever reach the site. To avoid our security, fraudsters will sometimes attempt to recruit genuine sellers to unknowingly help them scam others. They do this by convincing the user that they are also genuine but need help posting an ad, often in exchange for giving the user something they want. Although a rare occurrence, recruitment scams can appear as a job posting, property listing, or a singular item.

Recognising Recruitment Scams

Along with all of the typical scam red flags, recruitment scams are recognisable because they all have one thing in common: the person posting the ad isn’t the actual seller. In most cases, they will say something along the lines of ‘this item isn’t mine, but …’ or ‘contact the seller at this phone number…’

If they’re posting on behalf of a close friend, family member or neighbour, that’s fine. However, if they don’t know the seller well, they may not realise that they’ve been recruited by someone with less than honest intentions.

Avoiding Being Recruited

The best way to avoid being recruited is to not post ads on behalf of anyone that you don’t know and trust completely. If you are contacted by anyone that asks you to post an ad on their behalf, especially with the promise of a great deal, don’t respond. Not only will their offer be fake, but the ad they ask you to post could make you an unwitting accomplice.

If anyone you don’t know asks you to post an ad on their behalf, please contact our customer support team to let us know.

Title: Quick Safety Tips
Summary: Our quick-read guide to staying safe on Gumtree.
Description__c:
While most members of Gumtree have good experiences, it’s important to stay alert and educated about how to stay safe.

Know the Market

It’s important to know what the average cost of the item you’re looking for is in comparison to the ad you’re viewing. If it’s drastically less than similar items, be careful. Fraudsters often post a once-in-a-lifetime deal to pull in as many people as possible. The common saying stands: if it’s too good to be true, it probably is.

Do Your Research

If you’re buying an item, get to know what normally comes with it and make sure that all the parts you’ll need are there. For high-valued items, it’s also important to know what replicas look like and how to tell if it’s genuine.

If you’re looking into a service, job, or anything offered by a business, look up the company online. Make sure that their address and phone number check out. If available, look up some online reviews.

Don’t Give Out Personal Information

When speaking to individuals online, it’s important to be cautious when giving out information. Never give out your identification or banking details unless you are 100% sure that you’re speaking with the real company. Note: Gumtree’s customer service team will never ask for your identification, passwords, or banking details.

Meet in Person Before Paying

A Fraudster’s greatest tool is that online translations are anonymous. Don’t provide any money until after you’ve met them in person and had a chance to inspect the item. We recommend that you meet during the day in a busy, public location like a coffee shop.

Choose Safe Payment Methods

Many forms of money transfer can be faked or are hard to reverse should anything go wrong. If you can’t use cash, use safer methods such as PayPal and make sure that the payment has been processed before trading the item.

Trust Your Gut

Sometimes a sale just seems off. If anything isn’t sitting right with you, don’t be afraid to walk away. You are not obligated to follow through with a transaction even if you’ve already agreed to a price.

Note:

  • Gumtree is a local classifieds site and not all ads are reviewed before going live to site.
  • Gumtree does not offer any sort of protection programs for Gumtree items. Any emails or websites that talk about such systems are scams, even if they may have the Gumtree logo. If you receive any emails promoting these services, please forward the message to us.
  • This article is intended to serve as a quick overview of online safety. For more in-depth information, please browse our full Safety section

Title: Dealer Auction - Payments FAQs
Summary: Payments FAQs
Description__c:
Payment 

When do I receive the money for my car?

The dealer will organise an inspection upon collection. Assuming the car is as described then the dealer will transfer you the money via an agreed payment method. 

Will Gumtree or the dealer pay me?

The payment will come directly from the purchasing dealership, so no middlemen involved. Gumtree does not buy vehicles.

What happens to any remaining finance I have on the car?

If the dealer is settling the finance for you, you will need to provide a valid finance settlement letter showing the settlement figure and agreement reference. The dealer will pay the outstanding finance amount first and then the remaining balance will be transferred to your bank account. 

If you are paying off the finance yourself, you will be asked to provide a letter showing that the finance has been settled. The dealer will then transfer the funds into your bank account.

If the amount owed to the finance company is greater than the price of the vehicle, the dealer will contact you on how to proceed.

What happens if a Dealer can’t offer instant payment?

While most dealers offer instant payment, larger dealerships may have their own accounting systems that require additional processing time. Just a heads-up!

If the dealer you're working with doesn't offer instant payment, they will most likely provide you with a legally binding Proof of Purchase document to finalise the transaction.

 

Please note that our dealers transfer funds exclusively to UK bank accounts for security reasons. International accounts are currently not accepted.

Title: Protecting Pets by Making Our Pets Category Harder to Use - 2018 Statement
Summary: Read more about our work with animal advocacy groups and the actions Gumtree has taken to protect pets traded on the site.
Description__c:
Thank you for your interest in reading more about why, as of August 2018, Gumtree has introduced a charge for all adverts listed in our pets category.

For many of our users, the introduction of a paywall on Gumtree, even if it’s solely confined to pets will represent a major shift from our traditionally ‘free for all users’ model. As the UK’s number one classifieds site, with an 18-year history, the decision to introduce a charge has not been taken lightly, and from now on users who choose to list a pet advertisement on Gumtree will be charged a nominal fee.

A complicated issue

The truth is that the buying and selling of pets online is a contentious and emotional issue. While we are known as a nation of animal lovers there continues to be a small minority who look to exploit pets for financial gain, with no regard for their health, wellbeing or safety. These people are criminals, and many have very understandably called for an outright ban on the sale of animals online.

But, through our ongoing work with the relevant authorities and stakeholders – such as the Pet Advertising Advisory Group (PAAG) and the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (DEFRA) – we know that a blanket ban is, unfortunately, not that simple. The reality is that without strong enforcement the sale of pets would be pushed underground; out of sight of animal welfare bodies and policing/standards organisations who currently work hard to ensure standards are met. New sites selling pets would also likely then emerge and, unlike Gumtree, may not be as willing to engage with standards that seek to improve the welfare of the animals involved.

So, in a bid to deter unscrupulous operators from misusing the platform and to discourage the ‘casual’ trading of animals online we have introduced this new paywall. Based on the experience of one of our sister sites, Kijiji Canada, we believe this will be successful as forcing users to pay even a small amount will reduce the number of pets sold unscrupulously online, sometimes in a rather ‘casual’ manner, which is in line with Gumtree’s long-term ambition. It will also enhance the ability of law enforcement to track down users who are engaged in suspected illegal activity.

The necessary next step

At Gumtree we have always taken our responsibilities towards protecting animal welfare seriously. We work with a number of animal welfare charities, including the RSPCA, and we have been an active contributor to the work of PAAG – which brings animal welfare groups, vets, trade associations and online classified sites together to promote responsible pet advertising - for a number of years. Gumtree itself meets the 18 minimum standards set out by PAAG for websites offering pets for sale via online adverts to meet, which help ensure that safety standards are adhered to, and more animals are treated with respect and care.

This next step in creating a paywall for the pets category is a measure we have imposed on ourselves not because we are required to do so by government or our colleagues in the animal welfare industry, but because we believe it is the right thing to do. Gumtree is, and always has been, firmly committed to making sure our platform is as safe as possible for rehoming pets and this measure marks the latest milestone in our journey to improve safety for Gumtree users.

If we don’t convince you…

Don’t use us. It is everyone’s responsibility to ensure the welfare of animals in the UK and if you don’t feel comfortable selling your pets on Gumtree please look to accredited local shelters or rehoming centres instead. You can find additional options on the PAAG and RSPCA websites.

For additional questions about the Gumtree pet paywall, or other issues, please contact us for more information.

If you’re posting ticket ads on the site you need to know about these rules. Re-selling tickets can sometimes be tricky, so read about it to make sure you’re not breaking the law.

If you’re selling tickets make sure you have actual tickets, not e-tickets. These are not allowed on the site.
