Title: Dealer Auction - Selling Your Car FAQs
Summary: Selling your car
Description__c:
Selling your car

What is the difference between car buying websites (e.g. We Buy Any Car) and Dealer Auction?

Gumtree’s Dealer Auction offers a different service compared to car buying websites. While car buying websites directly purchases your car, Dealer Auction connects private sellers with dealers who will make offers on your vehicle through an auction format. This means you are more likely to receive a higher price. Dealer Auction collects more information upfront about your car, which in turn means your offer is less likely to be re-negotiated down.

Is it possible to sell a left-hand drive (LHD) car on Dealer Auction?

Dealers in the Dealer Auction network typically do not purchase imported vehicles, including left-hand drive (LHD) cars. The challenge lies in tracing the complete history of such vehicles within the UK market.

Does selling via Dealer Auction require a lot of effort?

No, selling your vehicle through Dealer Auction is a straightforward process. Simply create a regular listing, complete the additional information and accept or reject the final offer.

How does Gumtree secure the highest offer from dealers?

Gumtree finds your highest offer by allowing our network of dealers to compete in the auction. Dealers submit their offers based on the information and condition of your vehicle, and we’ll send you the highest offer above your reserve price when the auction closes.

How do dealers see information about my car?

When you provide all the necessary information and photos of your vehicle, dealers in our network review this information. 

Who purchases my car?

Gumtree does not directly purchase your vehicle. Instead, our platform connects you with dealers. The dealer with the winning bid will inspect your car. Assuming both seller and dealer are happy with the final offer, the dealer will purchase the car from you directly.

Do you have to accept an offer?

No, as a private seller you have the freedom to accept or decline offers based on your preferences. You are in control of the selling process and can decide whether or not to contact the dealer to accept their offer. 

What happens if my car does not meet the criteria to sell through Dealer Auction?

We will not be able to inform you if your vehicle is not eligible for sale through Dealer Auction. 

My car is a write-off. Can I sell it through Dealer Auction?

Dealers participating in Dealer Auction generally do not purchase vehicles that have been classified as category A, B, C, D, or S or N write-offs. However, we would encourage you to post a listing on Gumtree, advertising to private sellers and disclosing the relevant category your vehicle falls into. 

Can I sell a vehicle on finance?

Yes, however you will need to provide more information about the settlement amount and when the settlement amount is valid until.

Why is it important to take photos in a specific way?

Taking good quality photos of your vehicle is crucial for maximising offers and higher prices from dealers. You are recommended to take photos in a specific way to allow dealers to assess the vehicle's condition accurately and make more competitive offers. Failure to do so might result in the final offer changing upon inspection. 

How many photos should I take of my car?

To list your car for sale in Dealer Auction, we advise a total of 16 photos. These should cover the exterior (back, front, left side, right side, front right, front left, back right, back left, interior back, interior front, dashboard, alloys/ wheels, all tire treads, and other important aspects of your vehicle. Any damage should also be captured.

 

What photos do I need to take?

Please refer to the guide here for more information.

How do I upload the new images to my listing?

You can easily take the necessary photos using your smartphone or a camera. After you have taken the photos, head to manage my ads on Gumtree and edit your listing. The new photos will be automatically updated on the auction. 
 

I have already taken photos of my car. Can I upload these?

It depends. We require a good quality set of photos for your vehicle. This ensures consistency and enables dealers to evaluate your vehicle accurately. Assuming you have followed the guide here then you may use these photos and upload them in the normal posting experience on Gumtree. Otherwise we will need you to take a new set and upload or re-upload them to your listing via ‘manage my ads’ after you have posted your vehicle. 

Can I take a video instead of photos?

No, at the moment, we only accept photos to maintain a consistent presentation of vehicles in our online sales.

Do I need to declare the condition such as wear and tear?

Yes, it is essential to declare any wear and tear on your vehicle. Dealers base their offers on the information provided in your vehicle's profile, including its condition.

Should I make a note of damage?

Yes, you should disclose any damage big or small. Providing accurate information about its condition helps dealers make fair offers.
For example stone chips, chips or cracks on your windscreen, damage to your alloy wheels including minor damages such as kerb scuffs or trim chips through to scratches on the bodywork, broken lights and dents.

What does ‘vehicle service history’ mean?

Your vehicle's service history is a record of all the maintenance work performed on it throughout its lifetime. It includes details of services, repairs, and any relevant documentation associated with its maintenance.

Where do I find my vehicle service history records?

You can usually find your vehicle's service history records in your service book. Alternatively, some manufacturers or retailers store service records online. Check the manufacturer or retailer's website for access to your vehicle's service history.

How and when do I share my ‘vehicle's service history’ records?

It is advisable to provide details of as many service records as possible, including both recent and past services. You will need to show these when the vehicle is being inspected.

Can Gumtree find my vehicle's service history for me?

Unfortunately, we are unable to obtain your vehicle's service history on your behalf. It is the responsibility of the seller to provide accurate information and documentation.

What happens if the vehicle isn’t as described?

So long as you have accurately provided information about your vehicle then the dealer should not attempt to renegotiate the offer. 

If the vehicle is not as described or there are discrepancies which have a knock-on effect on the price, then dealers have the right to withdraw their offer or make a new offer.

Title: Reporting Reply & Text Fraud
Summary: Steps to report reply & text- based fraud attempts.
Description__c:
At Gumtree, your security is a key priority. We act on tips from our user community in an attempt to ensure that only legitimate activity is taking place. This is driving fraudsters to be ever more creative and to find new ways to connect with Gumtree users, such as via their mobile phone number. They'll try tricking you by sending fake SMS messages via the internet asking to be contacted via email. They do this because they wish to stay off our radar which they can't do if they reply through the usual channel; our reply email system.  

If you received an SMS scam reply, report it to 7726 (SPAM) on your handheld device and block the phone number to prevent them from contacting you again. To report to 7726, just forward the message. You will then be asked in a follow up text to provide the number that sent you the scam.

If you received a suspicious email through your Gumtree replies, please report this to our Customer Service Team so we can remove their access to our site and keep them from trying this on others. When making your report, please provide us with the ad ID associated with the reply, the suspect email address, and the name of the person you were interacting with. From your personal email inbox you can block the fraudsters masked Gumtree email address to prevent them from contacting you again.

Title: How the Tenant Fees Act 2019 Affects You
Summary: The Tenant Fees Act 2019 made some important changes to what types of fees you can be charged when renting.
Description__c:
With the introduction of the Tenant Fees Act 2019, there are new restrictions on the types of fees that property owners can charge when renting out a residential property. This act will affect new tenancies and renewals of tenancies after 1st June 2019.

Property owners may still request tenants pay the following types of fees:

  • Rent
  • Refundable deposits capped at five to six weeks’ rent (depending on the yearly rent totals
  • Refundable holding deposits capped at one week’s rent
  • Payments for early termination of tenancy (when requested by the tenant
  • Payments for utilities, communication services, TV licence and Council Tax
  • Default fees for late rent payments
  • Default fees for lost keys or secure entry devices

New requests for other types of payments such as fees for applications, arranging the viewing, or doing reference checks are now unlawful if charged after 1st June 2019. However, if other types of fees were listed within a contract signed prior to 1st June 2019, then these fees can still be charged up until 31st May 2020, or until the contract is renewed. For full understanding, please read through the legislature page.

Note: These rules only apply to residential properties. Commercial properties for rent are not covered by the Tenant Fees Act 2019.

If you see any private rental ads requesting these types of fees, please report it to our customer support team as well as to your local Trading Standards office.

Title: Third Party Code of Business Conduct and Ethics
Summary: Third Party Code of Business Conduct and Ethics
Description__c:
1. Introduction

Gumtree is committed to conducting business ethically, maintaining safe working conditions, and advancing social and environmental responsibility. Accordingly, Gumtree expects all businesses and individuals that it works with (“Third Party” or “Third Parties”) to abide by the principles outlined in this Third Party Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (“Code”).

The Code applies to all businesses and individuals who do business with Gumtree. Third Parties must ensure that their subcontractors also comply with the principles set out in this Code.

 

2. Business Integrity

Personal Relationships: Third Parties will disclose any family or close personal relationships they may have with Gumtree workers, employees, contractors, directors, and officers (“personnel”) who are engaged in their business activities with Gumtree.

Business Courtesies: Third Parties may not give business courtesies that might influence, or appear to influence, the decision making of Gumtree personnel. If given at all, business courtesies must be modest and infrequent, and otherwise comply with Gumtree’s Gifts and Hospitality Policy.

Gifts: Acceptable gifts include modest items. It is imperative any gifts from Third Parties comply with Gumtree’s Gifts and Hospitality Policy. Cash, as well as cash equivalents such as gift cards or shopping vouchers in any value, are prohibited. Gifts that violate Gumtree’s Gifts and Hospitality Policy will either be returned to the Third Party or handled in a manner that complies with said policy.

Entertainment and Meals: Reasonable and customary meals or entertainment aimed at furthering the business relationship are permissible. However, it is essential that such business meals or entertainment comply with Gumtree’s Gifts and Hospitality Policy.

Business Opportunities, Commissions or Advantageous Arrangements: Third Parties will not offer any business opportunities, commissions, or advantageous arrangements, whether financial or otherwise, that could personally benefit Gumtree personnel.

Bribery: Third Parties may not offer, promise, give or accept anything of value as an inducement or reward for an improper act, or to influence someone in the performance of their role. Moreover, Third Parties are prohibited from engaging in any other forms of bribery, corruption, extortion, or embezzlement, including making facilitation payments. It is the responsibility of Third Parties to implement procedures to ensure compliance with applicable anti-bribery and corruption laws, including oversight of their subcontractors’ conduct.

Books and Records: Third Parties must ensure their accounting and financial records accurately reflect their business practices.

Fair Business, Advertising, and Competition: Third Parties will comply with all applicable fair business, advertising, and competition laws, including fair trading and competition laws.

Data Protection and Privacy: Third Parties will commit to protecting the legitimate privacy expectations and personal information of everyone they do business with, including suppliers, customers, consumers, and personnel. Third Parties will comply with privacy and information security laws and regulatory requirements when it comes to the collection, storage, processing, transmission and sharing of personal information.

Compliance with laws: Gumtree expects Third Parties to comply, and procure that their subcontractors comply, with all laws, statues, regulations and codes applicable to their business activities, regardless of whether these are explicitly referenced in this Code.

3. Labour and Human Rights

Gumtree expects its Third Parties to respect and protect fundamental human rights in accordance with the international standards outlined by the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Fundamental Conventions of the International Labor Organization. These include:

Discrimination: Third Parties will not engage in discrimination based on ethnicity, religious beliefs, national origin, ancestry, pregnancy status, gender or gender identity, age, marital status, disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic as defined by the law. Third parties will also provide reasonable accommodations to accommodate disabilities and religious practices.

Freely Chosen Employment: Any form of forced, bonded or indentured labour, as well as involuntary prison labour, is prohibited. Gumtree expects Third Parties to take steps to ensuring that there are no such practices in their supply chains.

Child Labour: No person will be employed younger than age 13, unless specifically permitted by law. Third Parties will not interfere with a child’s education by employing them in contravention of compulsory education laws. Third Parties may however engage in lawful and voluntary workplace apprenticeship programs, including student internships, provided they comply with all laws and regulations. Additionally, individuals under the age of 18 will not be assigned tasks that could potentially endanger their health, safety or overall well-being. 

Harassment or Abuse: Every individual will be treated with respect and dignity. No individual will be subject to any physical, sexual, psychological, or verbal harassment or abuse. 

Health and Safety: Third Parties will provide a safe and healthy work environment that mitigates the risk of accidents and injuries associated with, or arising from, work activities or facilities. 

Compensation and Working Conditions: Third Parties commit to providing just and equitable legal compensation, adhering to humane working conditions, including upholding reasonable work hours in accordance with laws and local norms. Additionally, Third Parties will promote and enhance opportunities for workers to earn a sustainable living wage.

Freedom of Association: Third Parties will respect and recognise the right of personnel to join and organise associations of their own choosing, and to bargain collectively. Personnel will not be subject to intimidation or harassment in the exercise of their right to join or to refrain from joining any association.

Work Authorisation: Third Parties will not knowingly engage individuals who do not possess the legal authorisation to work, as determined by law. 

Armed Conflicts: Third Parties will take reasonable steps to ensure that the resources utilised in the products and/or service that they offer Gumtree do not have any connection, direct or indirect, with entities or persons that support armed groups that perpetrate human rights abuses.

4. Environmental Responsibility

Gumtree is committed to making a positive environmental impact on the environment through its actions and holds its Third Parties to the same high standards. Gumtree actively seeks and favours Third Parties that offer eco-efficient and sustainable products and services. Gumtree encourages its Third Parties to embrace the following key priorities:

Eco-Efficiency: Third Parties should strive to maximize the eco-efficiency of products and services throughout their life cycle, from sourcing and manufacturing to distribution, transportation, use and end-of life considerations. This involves minimising or eliminating all forms of waste, including water and energy, at the source or through practices such as modifying processes, materials substitution, conservation, recycling, and re-using materials.

Hazardous Substances: Chemicals and other materials that pose environmental hazards are to be identified and managed to ensure their safe handling, transportation, storage, use, recycling or reuse and disposal.

Wastewater and Solid Waste: Wastewater and solid waste generated from operations, industrial processes and sanitation facilities are to be characterised, monitored, controlled, and treated as necessary before discharge and disposal. prior to discharge or disposal.

Air Emissions: Air emissions of volatile organic chemicals, aerosols, corrosives, particulates, ozone depleting substances and combustion by-products resulting from operations are to be characterised, monitored, controlled, and treated as required prior to discharge.

Environmental Permits and Reporting: Third Parties are responsible for obtaining and maintaining all required environmental permits, approvals and registrations, and ensuring they adhere to operational and reporting requirements.  

Data Requests and Reporting: Gumtree may periodically request data to support its environmental reporting requirements. Gumtree kindly asks for cooperation in what is a collective effort to improve environmental reporting and performance.

5. Cooperation with Regulators

Third Parties will cooperate with regulatory authorities, including, but not limited to, inquiries, audits, reviews or investigations related to their business activities in connection with Gumtree. 

6. Artificial Intelligence (AI)

Third Parties will commit to the responsible use and development of AI systems in a manner that aligns with Gumtree’s AI principles, which include:

  • Data Privacy and Confidentiality: Ensuring the secure and lawful handling of personal data, and the protection of sensitive information.
  • Values and Fairness: Respecting the rule law, human rights, democratic values and diversity.
  • Transparency: Maintaining openness in the utilisation of AI system.
  • Accountability: Taking responsibility for the actions and decisions made by AI systems.

7. Communication

External Communication Integrity: Third Parties are expected to refrain from knowingly disseminating false, inaccurate or misleading information, whether through press releases, product or service advertisements, or any other medium.

Reporting Unethical or Improper Conduct: This Code governs the conduct of Gumtree personnel in alignment with Gumtree’s workplace policies, procedures, and agreements. If a Third Party suspects that the conduct or actions of Gumtree personnel may be unethical or improper, we strongly encourage the Third Party to report their concerns to Gumtree’s compliance team via email at askethics@gumtree.com. Anonymous reports can also be submitted through Gumtree’s third-party managed Whistleblowing Helpline, available via phone or web form.

Reporting Code Violations: Third Parties are required to promptly inform Gumtree of any breaches of this Code. Such notifications should be submitted without delay, as soon as the Third Party becomes aware of any violations, to the following email address: askethics@gumtree.com.

Reporting Regulatory Inquiries, Audits, Reviews, or Investigations: Third Parties shall promptly inform Gumtree of any regulatory inquiries, audits, reviews, or investigations concerning their business activities associated with Gumtree. Such notifications should be provided without delay as soon as the Third Party becomes aware of the inquiry, audit, review, or investigation and should be directed to askethics@gumtree.com.

Title: Staying Safe in our Jobs Category
Summary: Tips for staying safe in our Jobs Category.
Description__c:
Whether you’re looking for your next hire or seeking a new job opportunity, we have top tips to make sure you connect to the right role / employee. 

For Jobseekers

At Gumtree, we really want to help you find that great new job, so we have put together some advice to help you find work safely:

Do your Research

Before you send an application for a vacancy, do some research into the recruiter. This will help you prepare for an interview and allow you to make sure the business is a right fit for you and your skills. Legitimate recruiters will normally have a professional business email domain, landline phone number, can be found on companies house website and will have business premises. 

Ask Questions

Ask lots of questions about the role you are applying for, especially if you get to meet any current employees. You will want to know the exact details of what your day to day responsibilities will be. If a potential employer is vague about the details of the position, you should proceed with caution.

Sending Sensitive Information

Never provide sensitive information, like your bank account details or personal ID including copies of your passport or driving licence, when applying for a job. This information should only be provided once you’ve accepted an offer from the company, or when you’ve met your employer in person and verified their identity. 

Common Signs of Fraud

Unfortunately, there are some people who will advertise roles that do not exist. If you have reason to believe a role is not real or suspicious, please report it to us by using the ‘report ad’ button. Here are some common signs of fraudulent job ads:
 
  • the employer cannot be properly researched, and does not wish to meet face to face for interview
  • you are asked to make advanced payment for a background check (such as DBS) or uniform. Information on background checks can be found at this Government page
  • you are asked to call a premium rate phone number. These normally use the prefixes 070 or 090. You should always ask the employer to call you.
  • you are asked to download documents such as an application pack. You should only make downloads from a trusted source and ensure that when you open any files, including email attachments, you scan them first with up to date antivirus software.

For Recruiters/Employers

References & Checks 

Any employer, whatever the role should always check references and speak to past employers. However, there are some roles, such as childcare, where you may need to perform extra due diligence when recruiting someone into a position.

What should you ask for: 
  • Past references from at least 2 employers
  • DBS Check 

 A disclosure or DBS check (formerly known as a CRB check) is a background check on a potential employee designed to help prevent unsuitable people from working with vulnerable groups, such as children.

The UK Government website gives plenty of advice on what type of DBS check is right for you as an employer, as well as support and guidance on how to complete the check. 

If you are a recruiter in Scotland, similar guidance can be found here.

Recruiters in Northern Ireland can find guidance here.

If you ever have reason to believe you have received an unsuitable application or have concerns for the welfare of an individual we urge you to report it to the most relevant authority and contact our customer support team.
